definition_zh: 迹象；表明；指示；（医学）体征、适应证；读数
definition_en: a sign that shows something is true or likely, or the act of pointing something out
core_image: 一根手指指向远处，所有人顺着它看过去
scene: 客厅窗前，全家人盯着电视里的台风路径图，画面一帧帧更新。There was no indication that the storm would turn inland until the barometer fell.
sceneCN: 这里 indication 是「迹象」（第 1 个义项：显示某事可能属实的信号）；句意：在气压计下降之前，没有任何迹象表明风暴会转向内陆。图中可辨识物件：气压计指针、窗外压低的云层、指向地图的手指。

pos.zh: 迹象；表明；指示；体征；适应证

senses.title: A sign that something is so
senses.definition: a piece of evidence that suggests a fact or a likely development
senses.definitionCN: 暗示某事实或可能发展的证据
senses.example: There is no indication that the trend will reverse.
senses.exampleCN: 没有迹象表明这一趋势会逆转。
senses.why: Indicare means 'to point out'. An indication is a finger pointed at a fact, and the viewer must still read what it points to.
senses.whyCN: indicare 意为“指出”。indication 就是指向事实的一根手指，而观看者仍须读懂它指向什么。

senses.title: The act of pointing something out
senses.definition: the act of stating or showing that something is the case
senses.definitionCN: 陈述或显示某事如此的行为
senses.example: His indication of the exit saved us time.
senses.exampleCN: 他指出出口，替我们省了时间。
senses.why: The suffix -ation makes this the act itself, not the sign. Someone performs the pointing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ation 使这个词指行为本身，而非标志。是某人在做指向动作。

senses.title: A medical sign
senses.definition: in medicine, an observable sign that points to a condition
senses.definitionCN: 医学中指向某种病情的可观察体征
senses.example: Fever is one indication of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 发热是感染的一种体征。
senses.why: A clinical sign is a finger aimed at a hidden cause. The cause remains invisible; only the pointing is visible.
senses.whyCN: 临床体征是一根指向隐藏病因的手指。病因仍然不可见，可见的只有这次指向。

senses.title: A reading on an instrument
senses.definition: a value shown by a gauge or meter
senses.definitionCN: 计量仪表显示的数值
senses.example: The dial gave no indication of pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 表盘没有显示压力读数。
senses.why: The needle is a literal finger on a scale. The instrument indicates, and the reading is the indication.
senses.whyCN: 指针就是落在刻度上的一根真实手指。仪表在指示，读数就是这次指示。

senses.title: A signal or gesture
senses.definition: a gesture or signal intended to convey a message
senses.definitionCN: 意在传达讯息的手势或信号
senses.example: A nod was his indication that we should begin.
senses.exampleCN: 一个点头就是他示意我们开始的信号。
senses.why: Here the pointing is bodily and immediate. Nothing is written; the message is delivered by a movement.
senses.whyCN: 这里的指向是身体性的、即时的。没有文字，讯息由一个动作递出。

senses.title: A hint in speech or manner
senses.definition: a subtle hint given in conversation rather than a direct statement
senses.definitionCN: 交谈中给出的细微暗示，而非直接陈述
senses.example: He gave a slight indication that he was unhappy.
senses.exampleCN: 他给了个细微暗示，表示自己不高兴。
senses.why: The finger is only half raised. The word marks a signal deliberately kept below the level of a statement.
senses.whyCN: 手指只抬起一半。这个词标记的是一个被刻意压在陈述线以下的信号。

senses.title: Evidence pointing to a conclusion
senses.definition: in the phrase 'there is every indication', evidence strong enough to support an expectation
senses.definitionCN: 在“种种迹象表明”这一说法中，强到足以支持某种预期的证据
senses.example: There is every indication that the talks will succeed.
senses.exampleCN: 种种迹象表明会谈将会成功。
senses.why: The phrase weighs a set of fingers all pointing the same way. Indication becomes the collective direction of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法称量一组都指向同一方向的手指。indication 成了证据的集体方向。

senses.title: A reason to use a treatment
senses.definition: in medicine, a condition that makes a particular treatment appropriate
senses.definitionCN: 医学中使某种治疗变得合适的病情
senses.example: The scan gave a clear indication for surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描结果给出了明确的手术适应证。
senses.why: Here the pointing goes the other way: the condition points at the treatment, licensing the doctor to act.
senses.whyCN: 这里的指向反了过来：病情指向治疗，从而授权医生行动。

intro.en: Indication comes from Latin indicare, 'to point out'. It is built from in- plus dicare, 'to proclaim', and is related to index, the pointing finger. Every sense keeps that gesture: something is aimed at, and the viewer must read the aim.
intro.cn: indication 来自拉丁语 indicare“指出”。它由 in- 加 dicare“宣告”构成，与 index（食指、索引）同族。每个义项都保留那个手势：某物被指向，而观看者必须读懂指向。

items.en: Dicare meant 'to proclaim, to dedicate'. Its relation to dicere 'to say' is generally accepted, but the exact prehistoric division between the two verbs is uncertain.
items.cn: dicare 意为“宣告、奉献”。它与 dicere“说”的关系一般被接受，但两个动词在史前期的具体分化来源不确定。

items.en: Index meant 'a pointer, a sign, the forefinger'. The plural indices kept the same stem that produced indicate. This is why an index and an indication both point.
items.cn: index 意为“指示者、标志、食指”。复数 indices 保留的词干正产生了 indicate。索引与迹象都指方向，原因就在这里。

items.en: In- plus dicare gave indicare, 'to point out, to show, to give a sign'. The verb was used of fingers, of evidence and of prices.
items.cn: in- 加 dicare 构成 indicare“指出、显示、给出信号”。这个动词既用于手指，也用于证据与价格。

items.en: The noun indicatio named the act of pointing out. Latin medical writers already used it for symptoms that point to a disease.
items.cn: 名词 indicatio 指指出某物的行为。拉丁医学作者已用它指指向疾病的症状。

items.en: English borrowed indication through French. Early uses concerned both 'a hint' and 'a symptom', and the medical sense has never left.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入 indication。早期用法兼指“暗示”与“症状”，医学义从未离开这个单词。

items.en: Clinical indication, indication for surgery and instrument indications fixed the word in medicine and engineering, where a sign licenses an action.
items.cn: 临床指征、手术适应证与仪表读数使这个词固定于医学与工程，在这些领域里，一个信号就是行动的依据。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, this noun and the instrument noun. The meaning group compares words for signs and evidence.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、本名词与仪器名词；词义组比较表示迹象与证据的词。

entries.definition: to point out or show. It is the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指出或显示。它是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: a gauge or a measurable sign. It is the thing that points, while indication is the pointing or the pointed-at fact.
entries.definitionCN: 仪表或可测量的标志。它是做指向的东西，而 indication 是指向动作或被指的事实。

entries.definition: an alphabetical list, a number expressing change, or the forefinger. It shares the pointing stem.
entries.definitionCN: 按字母排列的清单、表示变化的数字，或食指。它共享“指向”的词干。

entries.definition: anything that suggests the presence of something. It is the broad everyday word; indication is more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示某物存在的任何东西。它是宽泛的日常词，indication 更正式。

entries.definition: a change in the body that points to a disease. It matches sense 03 specifically.
entries.definitionCN: 身体上指向疾病的变化。它专门对应第 3 义项。

entries.definition: facts offered to support a claim. It is stronger than indication and carries the weight of proof.
entries.definitionCN: 为支持某主张而提供的事实。它比 indication 更强，带有证明的分量。

entries.definition: an indirect suggestion. It is close to sense 06 and is always deliberately understated.
entries.definitionCN: 间接的提示。它接近第 6 义项，且总是刻意压低力度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build indication from in- plus dicare, 'to proclaim', and keep the pointing finger and the index card in view.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 in- 加 dicare“宣告”搭起 indication，并让指向的手指与索引卡始终在眼前。

normal.en: See in- + dicare: to proclaim towards something. An indication is a proclamation aimed at a fact.
normal.cn: 看成 in- 加 dicare：朝某物宣告。indication 就是指向某个事实的宣告。

normal.en: Picture a finger pointing at a distant hill: the hill is the fact, the finger is the indication.
normal.cn: 想象一根手指指向远处的山：山是事实，手指是迹象。

normal.en: An index is a book's pointing finger; an indication is evidence's pointing finger.
normal.cn: 索引是书的指向手指；迹象是证据的指向手指。

normal.en: In medicine, a symptom points at a cause the doctor cannot yet see.
normal.cn: 在医学里，症状指向医生尚看不见的病因。

normal.en: When there is every indication, many fingers point the same way.
normal.cn: 当“种种迹象表明”时，是许多手指都指向同一方向。

abstract.en: Keep one gesture: aim, and let another read the aim.
abstract.cn: 只记一个手势：指过去，让别人读懂所指。

abstract.en: Treat the word as weaker than proof and stronger than a guess.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作比证据弱、比猜测强的东西。

abstract.en: Notice that the same word covers a raised finger and a falling barometer: both are pointers.
abstract.cn: 注意同一个词既覆盖抬起的手指，也覆盖下降的气压计：两者都是指向器。

examples.en: The survey gives a useful indication of public mood.
examples.cn: 这项调查为了解公众情绪提供了有用的迹象。

examples.en: There is every indication that the policy is working.
examples.cn: 种种迹象表明这项政策正在奏效。

examples.en: The doctor found no indication for further surgery.
examples.cn: 医生认为没有进一步手术的适应证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“印地开神”：印度街头的开示神像用手一指，众人顺着看过去——这就是指示、迹象。

root: 拉丁语 indicare“指出、显示”（in- 朝向 + dicare 宣告），名词 indicatio；与 index“食指、索引”同出“指向”词干。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of indication is a pointing. Sometimes the finger is a symptom, sometimes a needle, sometimes a nod, sometimes a half-raised hint, sometimes a whole body of evidence, and sometimes a condition that points at a treatment. The word never contains the conclusion; it contains the direction in which to look.
sensesIntro.cn: indication 的每个义项都是一次指向。有时手指是症状，有时是仪表指针，有时是一个点头，有时是抬到一半的暗示，有时是整组证据，有时是病情指向某种治疗。这个词从不包含结论，它包含的是该往哪里看。

core.en: A pointing that tells another where to look.
core.cn: 一次指向，告诉别人该往哪里看。

branches.en: EVIDENCE: signs and the collective weight of signs.
branches.cn: 证据：迹象与迹象的集体分量。

branches.en: GESTURE: the act of pointing and a signal given by hand.
branches.cn: 手势：指向动作与用手给出的信号。

branches.en: HINT: a sign deliberately kept below the level of a statement.
branches.cn: 暗示：被刻意压在陈述线以下的信号。

branches.en: MEDICINE: a symptom pointing to a cause, a condition licensing treatment.
branches.cn: 医学：指向病因的症状，以及授权治疗的病情。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT: a needle's reading.
branches.cn: 仪表：指针的读数。

intro.en: Indication is indicare plus -atio. The items below gather the pointing family, including index, which looks different but shares the same stem.
intro.cn: indication 是 indicare 加 -atio。下列条目汇总“指向”词族，包括形似不同却共享同一词干的 index。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the pointing verb and the pointer noun. They explain why an index and an indication belong to one family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出指向动词与指示者名词。它们解释了为什么索引与迹象属于同一家族。

items.meaning: a sign; the act of pointing out
items.example: The indication was easy to miss.
items.exampleCN: 这个迹象很容易被忽略。

items.example: The figures indicate a slow recovery.
items.exampleCN: 这些数字表明复苏缓慢。

items.example: The indicator moved into the red zone.
items.exampleCN: 指示器进入了红色区域。

items.example: The tone is indicative of trouble.
items.exampleCN: 这种语气表明有麻烦。

items.meaning: a list or a number that points to change
items.meaningCN: 指向变化的清单或数字
items.example: The price index rose sharply.
items.exampleCN: 价格指数大幅上升。

items.structure: plural of index, from Latin indices
items.example: Both indices point to slower growth.
items.exampleCN: 两个指数都指向增长放缓。

items.meaning: pointing to context, as a word like 'here'
items.meaningCN: 指向语境的，如“这里”这类词
items.example: Pronouns are indexical expressions.
items.exampleCN: 代词是指示性表达。

items.meaning: in a way that serves as a sign
items.example: The sample was indicatively small.
items.exampleCN: 这个样本小得只能算个示意。

definition_zh: 个人的；单独的；独特的；个人；个体
definition_en: relating to one single person or thing, separate and distinct, or a single human being considered on their own
core_image: 一件不能再被切开的东西：切到它这里就到底了
scene: 球场边，教练挨个点名叫队员出列，目光在每个人身上停留片刻。The coach praised every individual on the team for trying his best.
sceneCN: 这里 individual 是「个人、个体」（第 4 个义项：作为单个人来看的人）；句意：队里每一个个人都必须了解计划，不只是队长。图中可辨识物件：战术板、逐个点名的手指、球员。

pos.zh: 个人的；单独的；独特的；单个的
个人；个体；单个人或事物

collocations.zh: 私人（普通个人，非官方身份）

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Single and separate
senses.titleCN: 单独的：作为一个单位分开看
senses.definition: relating to one single person or thing, considered separately from the group
senses.definitionCN: 指单个的人或物，从群体中分开来看
senses.example: Each individual case must be judged on its own facts.
senses.exampleCN: 每个单独的案件都必须依其自身事实判断。
senses.why: Latin individuus is in- 'not' + dividuus 'divisible'. An individual is the point at which division stops, so the first sense is simply 'one that cannot be split further'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 individuus 由 in-“不”+ dividuus“可分的”构成。individual 就是“分割停止的那一点”，因此第一个义项就是“无法再被切开的一个”。

senses.title: Distinctive and personal
senses.titleCN: 独特的：带有个人印记的
senses.definition: having a quality or style that is clearly one's own and different from others
senses.definitionCN: 具有明显属于自己、区别于他人的品质或风格
senses.example: The room has an individual character that no catalogue could copy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间有一种目录册无法复制的独特气质。
senses.why: Once a thing is separated from the group, its differences become visible. The word moves from 'single' to 'uniquely marked'.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物从群体中分开，它的差异就变得可见。这个词于是从“单个”转为“带有独特标记”。

senses.title: Intended for one person
senses.titleCN: 供一人用的：按个人配置
senses.definition: designed or intended for one person rather than for a group
senses.definitionCN: 为一个人而非一群人所设计或准备的
senses.example: The airline serves individual portions of ice cream.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司提供单人份的冰淇淋。
senses.why: This sense is recorded from 1889. The unit of distribution becomes one person, so the portion is cut to the size of an individual.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项自 1889 年有记录。分配单位变成了一个人，于是份额被切到“个体”的大小。

senses.title: A single human being
senses.titleCN: 个人：作为单个人来看的人
senses.definition: one human being, especially when considered apart from a group or society
senses.definitionCN: 一个人，尤指与群体或社会分开来看时
senses.example: The law protects the individual as well as the community.
senses.exampleCN: 法律既保护个人，也保护社群。
senses.why: The noun sense, recorded from the 1640s, applies the 'indivisible unit' idea to a person. Each person is a unit that cannot be dissolved into the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 名词义自 17 世纪 40 年代有记录，把“不可分的单位”这一观念用到了人身上。每个人都是无法被溶解进人群的单位。

senses.title: A biological individual
senses.titleCN: 生物个体：一个独立的生命单位
senses.definition: in biology, a single organism considered as a distinct unit
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中，作为独立单位看待的单个生物体
senses.example: The study tracked one hundred individual birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追踪了一百只单独的鸟。
senses.why: Biology needs a countable unit below the species and above the cell. The individual is that unit: one life that can be observed and counted.
senses.whyCN: 生物学需要一个低于物种、高于细胞的计数单位。individual 就是那个单位：一条可被观察与计数的生命。

senses.title: Informal: a person of a certain kind
senses.titleCN: （口语）某个家伙：带评价色彩的人
senses.definition: in colloquial use, a person, often with mildly negative or ironic judgement
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法中指一个人，常带轻微贬义或讽刺评价
senses.example: A rather odd individual was asking about you.
senses.exampleCN: 有个挺奇怪的家伙在打听你。
senses.why: The colloquial 'person' sense is attested from 1742. Calling someone 'an individual' distances them, as if viewing them as a specimen rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 口语“人”义自 1742 年有记录。把某人称作 an individual 会产生距离感，仿佛把他当作标本而不是人来看。

senses.title: Relating to one member's rights
senses.definition: relating to the rights, duties, or liberties of one person rather than a collective
senses.definitionCN: 指一个人的权利、义务或自由，而非集体的
senses.example: Individual rights must be balanced against public safety.
senses.exampleCN: 个人权利必须与公共安全相权衡。
senses.why: Political thought uses the word to mark the boundary between the person and the collective. The indivisible unit is also the unit that holds rights.
senses.whyCN: 政治思想用这个词标记个人与集体之间的边界。那个不可分的单位，也是持有权利的单位。

senses.title: An indivisible particle
senses.titleCN: 不可分的单元：原子式的个体
senses.definition: in older philosophy, an indivisible entity or atom
senses.definitionCN: 较旧哲学中，一个不可分的实体或原子
senses.example: The old philosophers argued that every body is made of individuals.
senses.exampleCN: 古代哲学家论证说，每个物体都由不可分的单元构成。
senses.why: Latin individuum as a noun meant 'an atom, an indivisible particle'. The atom is the limiting case of the word's literal meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 individuum 意为“原子、不可分的微粒”。原子正是这个词字面意义的极限情形。

senses.title: A distinct entity in a system
senses.definition: one distinct item treated as a unit within a larger system, such as a record or an account
senses.definitionCN: 在更大系统中被当作单位处理的一个独立项目，如一条记录或一个账户
senses.example: Each individual account is audited once a year.
senses.exampleCN: 每个单独的账户每年审计一次。
senses.why: The unit idea travels beyond people. Any system that must keep parts separate marks each one as an individual, whether it is a person, a record, or a cell.
senses.whyCN: “单位”观念可以走出人。任何必须把部分保持分开的系统，都会把每一项标记为 individual，不论是人、记录还是细胞。

intro.en: Individual is the negative of divisible: Latin in- 'not' + dividere 'divide'. Its first English use was theological, about the indivisible Trinity; the modern 'single person' sense is only about 400 years old.
intro.cn: individual 是 divisible 的否定式：拉丁语 in-“不”+ dividere“分开”。它最早的英语用法是神学的，指不可分的三位一体；现代“单个人”的义项只有约四百年历史。

items.en: First recorded as 'one and indivisible, inseparable', with reference to the Trinity. This original sense is now obsolete.
items.cn: 最早记录为“单一且不可分、不可分离”，用于指三位一体。这一最初义项如今已废弃。

items.en: Individualis was formed from Latin individuus 'indivisible', from in- 'not' + dividuus 'divisible'. The word was rare before c. 1600; the 15c. example may be an outlier.
items.cn: individualis 由拉丁语 individuus“不可分的”构成，后者来自 in-“不”+ dividuus“可分的”。这个词在 1600 年前并不常见；15 世纪的用例可能只是孤例。

items.en: Dividere 'to force apart, cleave, distribute' is dis- 'apart' + -videre 'to separate', from PIE *(d)uid- 'to separate, distinguish'. Individual therefore contains the idea of division by negating it. The roots must not be confused: indicare uses dicare 'proclaim', induce uses ducere 'lead', and individual uses dividere 'divide'.
items.cn: dividere“分开、劈开、分配”由 dis-“分开”+ -videre“分离”构成，来自原始印欧语 *(d)uid-“分开、区分”。因此 individual 是通过否定“分割”而包含分割观念的。这些词根不可混淆：indicate 用 dicare“宣告”，induce 用 ducere“引导”，individual 用 dividere“分开”。

items.en: The sense 'single, separate, of but one person or thing' appears. The word now answers the question 'which one, apart from the rest?'
items.cn: “单个的、分开的、只属于一个人或物的”义项出现。此时这个词回答的是“哪一个，与其余分开来看？”

items.en: The noun means 'a single human being' as opposed to a group. Latin individuum had already meant 'an atom, indivisible particle'.
items.cn: 名词指“单个人”，与群体相对。拉丁语 individuum 早已表示“原子、不可分的微粒”。

items.en: The sense 'intended for one person' is recorded in 1889. Individualism as a social philosophy dates from the mid-19c., and individual rights become a central political phrase.
items.cn: “供一人使用的”义项自 1889 年有记录。作为社会哲学的个人主义始于 19 世纪中期，individual rights 则成为核心政治短语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the divid- root; the near-meaning group separates 'one unit' from 'one person' and 'unique'.
note.cn: 形近组共享 divid- 词根；近义组区分“一个单位”“一个人”与“独特”。

entries.definition: impossible to divide. It shows the root meaning that individual has largely left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 无法分割的。它显出 individual 已大体遗落的词根本义。

entries.definition: the quality of being a distinct person with a character of one's own.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一个有自身性格的独立个体的性质；个性。

entries.definition: a social outlook that gives the individual priority over the collective.
entries.definitionCN: 把个人置于集体之上的社会观念；个人主义。

entries.definition: one only, not one of a group. It is simpler and does not carry the 'indivisible' idea.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一个，不是群体中的一员。它更简单，不带“不可分”的观念。

entries.definition: existing apart from others. It stresses distance, while individual stresses being a distinct unit.
entries.definitionCN: 与他人分开存在的。它强调距离，而 individual 强调是一个独立单位。

entries.definition: one specific person or thing rather than any other. It stresses selection rather than separateness.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的人或物，而非其他。它强调“选定”，而不是“分离”。

entries.definition: a human being. It is the ordinary word, while individual can sound formal or slightly distancing.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人。它是最普通的词，而 individual 可能显得正式或略带距离感。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases; the in- here means 'not', not 'into'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语；这里的 in- 是“不”，不是“进入”。

normal.en: in- 'not' + dividere 'divide': an individual is the unit that cannot be divided further.
normal.cn: in-“不”+ dividere“分开”：individual 就是无法再被分割的单位。

normal.en: divide, division and individual share the same root, but individual negates it.
normal.cn: divide、division、individual 共享同一词根，但 individual 对它作了否定。

normal.en: Individual rights treat each person as a unit that cannot be dissolved into the crowd.
normal.cn: individual rights 把每个人当作无法被溶解进人群的单位。

normal.en: An individual portion is cut to the size of one unit rather than the group.
normal.cn: individual portion 是按“一个单位”而非群体切分的份量。

normal.en: Calling someone an individual instead of a person adds a little distance, as if observing a specimen.
normal.cn: 把某人称作 individual 而不是 person，会加一点距离感，仿佛在观察一个标本。

abstract.en: Picture a loaf that can be sliced until only one crumb is left; the crumb that cannot be halved again is the individual.
abstract.cn: 想象一条面包可以被切片，直到只剩一粒碎屑；那粒无法再对半切的碎屑就是 individual。

abstract.en: Every crowd is an optical illusion: lower your eyes far enough and you see only individuals.
abstract.cn: 每一片人群都是一种错觉：把视线降得足够低，你只会看见一个又一个 individual。

abstract.en: Individuality is the scar left by separation: what makes you one thing also makes you unlike the others.
abstract.cn: individuality 是分离留下的印记：让你成为“一个”的东西，也让你不同于其他。

examples.en: The teacher gives individual attention to each learner.
examples.cn: 老师给每个学习者单独的关照。

examples.en: Each individual has a different reason for joining the course.
examples.cn: 每个人加入这门课的理由都不同。

examples.en: The survey interviews individuals rather than households.
examples.cn: 这项调查采访的是个人，而不是家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬地微丢”+“啊”——硬在地上微微丢了一块，只剩单个个体 → individual 个人、个体

root: 源自中世纪拉丁语 individualis“不可分的”，来自拉丁语 individuus（in-“不”+ dividere“分开”），核心是“切分到这里就停止的单一单位”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of individual, all built on one unit that cannot be divided further. That unit can be a person, an organism, a record, or an atom.
sensesIntro.cn: individual 的九个义项都建立在同一个“无法再被分割的单位”上。这个单位可以是人、生物体、记录，或原子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole that cannot be cut again without ceasing to be itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个整体，再切一刀就不再是它自己。

branches.en: ATOM: the literal limit case, an entity with no possible further division.
branches.cn: 原子：字面上的极限情形，一个无法再分的实体。

branches.en: COUNTABLE UNIT: biology, records and cases each need one unit that can be counted.
branches.cn: 可数单位：生物学、记录与案件都需要一个可计数的单位。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the unit is a human being, and that unit is the bearer of rights.
branches.cn: 人：这个单位是一个人，而这个人正是权利的持有者。

branches.en: ONE-PERSON USE: portions and arrangements are cut to the size of one unit.
branches.cn: 单人使用：份额与安排被切到一个单位的大小。

branches.en: DISTINCTION: separation makes difference visible, for praise or for ironic distance.
branches.cn: 区别：分离让差异可见，既可用于赞赏，也可用于讽刺性的距离。

intro.en: Individual is in- 'not' + divid- 'divide' + -ual. English adds -ity, -ism, -ist, -ize and -ly; the prefix here is privative, not locative.
intro.cn: individual 是 in-“不”+ divid-“分开”+ -ual。英语加 -ity、-ism、-ist、-ize、-ly；这里的前缀是否定性的，不是方位性的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is dividere 'to divide' and individuus 'indivisible'. Relatives include divide, division, dividend and subdivide.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 dividere“分开”与 individuus“不可分的”。同族词包括 divide、division、dividend、subdivide。

items.meaning: the quality of being a distinct person or thing
items.meaningCN: 个性；个体性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The school encourages individuality rather than uniformity.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校鼓励个性而非一律。

items.meaning: a belief that the individual takes priority over the group
items.meaningCN: 个人主义；认为个人优先于群体的观念
items.example: Individualism shapes much of the country's law.
items.exampleCN: 个人主义塑造了这个国家的大部分法律。

items.meaning: a person who acts independently or believes in individualism
items.meaningCN: 个人主义者；独立行事的人
items.example: She was an individualist who disliked committees.
items.exampleCN: 她是个不喜欢委员会的个人主义者。

items.meaning: marked by independent or self-directed behaviour
items.meaningCN: 个人主义的；强调独立自主的
items.example: The team culture was too individualistic for joint work.
items.exampleCN: 这种团队文化过于个人主义，不适合协作。

items.meaning: to make personal or suited to one person
items.example: The software individualizes each exercise.
items.exampleCN: 这款软件会为每道练习定制内容。

items.meaning: the process of making something personal
items.example: Individualization of treatment improves outcomes.
items.exampleCN: 治疗的个体化能改善结果。

items.example: Each file was checked individually.
items.exampleCN: 每个文件都被逐一检查。

items.meaning: to distinguish one thing from others; to become a separate self
items.meaningCN: 使区分；使成为独立个体（心理学术语）
items.example: Children individuate slowly from their parents.
items.exampleCN: 孩子会慢慢从父母那里形成独立自我。

items.meaning: the process of becoming a distinct individual
items.meaningCN: 个体化过程；成为独立个体的过程
items.example: Jung described individuation as a lifelong task.
items.exampleCN: 荣格把个体化描述为一项终身任务。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 不可分的；无法被分割的

definition_zh: 工业的；产业的；工业化的；从事工业的
definition_en: relating to industry, manufacturing, or the people and systems that produce goods in factories
core_image: 厂房里的传送带不停转动，成品排成队列向外送出
scene: 沿河的老厂房连成一片，烟囱林立，机器声日夜不停。The industrial belt along the river employed half the town.
sceneCN: 这里 industrial 是「工业的」（第 1 个义项：与工业或制造业相关的）；句意：沿河的工业带雇用了镇上半数人口；它的老纺织厂如今与新电子厂并立。图中可辨识物件：厂房、传送带、烟囱、电子元件。

pos.zh: 工业的；产业的；工业化的；从事工业的

senses.title: Relating to industry and manufacturing
senses.definition: connected with industry, especially the manufacturing of goods in factories
senses.definitionCN: 与工业相关的，尤指在工厂中制造商品
senses.example: The government published a report on industrial growth.
senses.exampleCN: 政府发布了一份关于工业增长的报告。
senses.why: Latin -alis means 'of or pertaining to'. Added to industry, industrial simply means 'of industry'; when industry came to mean factory manufacturing, the adjective followed it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 -alis 意为「属于某物的、与某物相关的」。加在 industry 上，industrial 就是「工业的」；当 industry 转指工厂制造业时，这个形容词也随之转义。

senses.title: Used in or for industry
senses.definition: made for use by industry, or operating on the scale of industry rather than a household
senses.definitionCN: 供工业使用的，或按工业而非家庭规模运作的
senses.example: Industrial chemicals must be stored under strict safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 工业化学品必须在严格的安全规则下储存。
senses.why: The adjective marks belonging: chemicals that belong to the industrial process, not the kitchen. The same pattern gives industrial diamonds and industrial glue.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记归属：属于工业流程而非厨房的化学品。同一模式也构成 industrial diamonds（工业钻石）与 industrial glue（工业胶）。

senses.title: Having a lot of industry
senses.titleCN: 工业发达的；工业密集的
senses.definition: describing a place that contains many factories and much manufacturing
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个拥有许多工厂和大量制造业的地方
senses.example: The industrial north has higher wages but worse air.
senses.exampleCN: 工业化的北方工资更高，但空气更差。
senses.why: A place can be named by what fills it. If industry fills a region, the region is industrial, just as a forested valley is wooded.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方可以用充满它的东西来命名。如果工业充满一个地区，这个地区就是 industrial，正如长满森林的山谷是 wooded。

senses.title: Relating to employers and workers
senses.definition: concerning the relationship between employers and employees, especially disputes and negotiations
senses.definitionCN: 关于雇主与雇员之间关系的，尤指争端与谈判
senses.example: Industrial relations in the plant have improved since the new manager arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理到任后，厂里的劳资关系有所改善。
senses.why: The relationship exists inside industry, so the adjective locates it: industrial relations are the relations of the industrial workplace, not relations between industries.
senses.whyCN: 这种关系存在于工业内部，所以形容词为其定位：industrial relations 是工业工作场所内部的关系，而非工业之间的关系。

senses.title: Concerning government policy toward industry
senses.definition: relating to official plans and measures that support, regulate, or restructure industry
senses.definitionCN: 与支持、规范或重组工业的官方计划与措施相关的
senses.example: Industrial policy in the region focuses on semiconductors.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的产业政策聚焦于半导体。
senses.why: Here industrial marks the object of policy: the policy is about industry. The adjective tells you what the noun governs, not who makes it.
senses.whyCN: 此处 industrial 标记政策的对象：政策是关于工业的。这个形容词说明名词管的是什么，而不是谁制定它。

senses.title: Characteristic of an industrial society
senses.titleCN: 工业社会的；工业时代的
senses.definition: belonging to the era or type of society whose economy and daily life are dominated by industry
senses.definitionCN: 属于经济与日常生活由工业主导的时代或社会类型的
senses.example: The industrial city replaced the market town as the typical settlement.
senses.exampleCN: 工业城市取代集镇成为典型的聚居形态。
senses.why: When industry dominates an age, the adjective can name the age itself: industrial society is the society shaped by industry, a label rather than a description of a single object.
senses.whyCN: 当工业主导一个时代时，这个形容词可以命名时代本身：industrial society 是由工业塑造的社会，是标签而非对单一事物的描述。

senses.title: Belonging to the secondary sector
senses.titleCN: 第二产业的；工业部门的
senses.definition: belonging to the sector of the economy that transforms raw materials into goods, as opposed to agriculture or services
senses.definitionCN: 属于把原材料转化为产品的经济部门，与农业或服务业相对
senses.example: Industrial employment fell as service jobs expanded.
senses.exampleCN: 随着服务业岗位扩张，工业就业下降。
senses.why: Statisticians classify an economy by adjectives: agricultural, industrial, service. The adjective turns a sector into a label, and the label becomes a noun-like category.
senses.whyCN: 统计学家用形容词给经济分类：农业的、工业的、服务业的。这个形容词把部门变成标签，而标签又近似名词范畴。

senses.title: Industrial shares on the stock market
senses.definition: the shares of industrial companies, used in the plural as a category on financial markets
senses.definitionCN: 工业公司的股票，在金融市场上以复数形式作为一类资产
senses.example: Investors moved money out of industrials and into technology.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者把资金从工业股转投科技股。
senses.why: This is an ellipsis: 'industrial shares' loses shares and keeps the adjective, which then behaves as a noun. English does this with many adjectives, as in valuables and chemicals.
senses.whyCN: 这是省略：industrial shares 省去 shares，只留形容词，形容词便充当名词。英语常用这种方式，如 valuables 与 chemicals。

senses.title: Bare, functional, machine-made in style
senses.titleCN: 工业风的；机器制造感的
senses.definition: having a plain, functional, machine-made look, as in industrial design or industrial music
senses.definitionCN: 具有朴素、功能化、机器制造观感的，如工业设计或工业音乐
senses.example: The loft kept its industrial look with exposed pipes and concrete walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这间 Loft 保留工业风，露出管道和混凝土墙。
senses.why: The metaphor drops the factory and keeps its manner: what looks as if it came from a factory, all bare function and metal, is called industrial.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻丢开工厂本身，只保留它的方式：看起来像从工厂出来、全是裸露功能与金属感的东西，就被称为 industrial。

intro.en: Industrial is industry plus the Latin adjective suffix -alis, which became English -al. French industriel was the model for the English word, and the manufacturing sense of industry made the adjective mean 'of factories'.
intro.cn: industrial 是 industry 加拉丁形容词后缀 -alis（在英语中变为 -al）构成。法语 industriel 是英语词的样板；industry 的制造业义使这个形容词意为「工厂的」。

items.en: industria meant 'diligence, activity, care'. Its deeper origin is uncertain and is generally reconstructed as indu- (in-) + struere 'to build', but this is not proven.
items.cn: industria 意为「勤勉、活动、用心」。其更深来源不确定，一般重构为 indu-（in-）+ struere「建造」，但并未得到证明。

items.en: industrius meant 'diligent, active'. It kept the personal sense of hard work, which English preserves in industrious.
items.cn: industrius 意为「勤勉的、活跃的」。它保留了个人勤奋这一意义，英语以 industrious 保存下来。

items.en: 18th-century French formed industriel from industrie to mean 'relating to manufacturing'. French was then the language of economic writing, so the model spread quickly.
items.cn: 18 世纪法语由 industrie 构成 industriel，意为「与制造业相关的」。当时法语是经济写作的语言，这一样板迅速传播。

items.en: English adopted industrial in the late 18th century, at first in phrases describing manufacturing. The word grew with the very thing it described.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪晚期采用 industrial，最初用于描述制造业的短语。这个词随它所描述的事物一同成长。

items.en: The phrase industrial revolution made the adjective the name of an era. From there industrial society, industrial city, and industrial age followed as standard labels.
items.cn: industrial revolution 这一短语使该形容词成为时代的名称。此后 industrial society、industrial city、industrial age 都成为标准标签。

items.en: In the 20th century industrial produced a noun plural, industrials, for industrial shares, and later described machine-made styles in design and music. These are ellipses and metaphors of the core sense.
items.cn: 20 世纪 industrial 产生名词复数 industrials，指工业股票；后来又在设计与音乐中描述机器制造的风格。这些都是核心义的省略与隐喻。

note.en: Group one shares the Latin base industria; group two is close in meaning but not cognate with it (manus + facere, Greek mekhane, and the compound mass-produce).
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词基 industria；第二组意义相近，但与它并非同源（manus + facere、希腊 mekhane，以及复合词 mass-produce）。

entries.definition: manufacturing as a sector, or diligent work; the noun from which industrial is formed
entries.definitionCN: 作为部门的制造业，或勤勉的工作；industrial 所由构成的名词

entries.definition: hard-working; it kept the 'diligence' sense of industria and never came to mean 'of factories'
entries.definitionCN: 勤劳的；它保留了 industria 的「勤勉」义，从未变成「工厂的」

entries.definition: having developed a large manufacturing base; the -ed form describes a result, while industrial describes a relation
entries.definitionCN: 已发展出大规模制造业的；-ed 形式描述结果，而 industrial 描述关系

entries.definition: an owner or manager of large industry; -ist names a person, not a quality
entries.definitionCN: 大型工业的所有者或管理者；-ist 命名人，而非性质

entries.definition: the making of goods on a large scale; it names the activity, while industrial describes what belongs to it
entries.definitionCN: 大规模制造商品；它命名活动，而 industrial 描述从属于该活动的事物

entries.definition: run or operated by machines; a mechanized process is one kind of industrial process
entries.definitionCN: 由机器运行或操作的；机械化的过程是工业过程的一种

entries.definition: made in large numbers by a standard process; it stresses quantity, not the whole industrial system
entries.definitionCN: 按标准流程大量制造的；强调数量，而非整个工业体系

entries.definition: relating to manual or factory workers; it describes people, while industrial can describe places, goods, or policies
entries.definitionCN: 与体力或工厂劳动者相关的；它描述人，而 industrial 可描述地点、商品或政策

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: industria 'diligence, activity' + -al 'of or pertaining to': industrial means 'of that activity', and the activity later became factory manufacturing.
normal.cn: industria「勤勉、活动」+ -al「与之相关的」：industrial 意为「与该活动相关的」，而该活动后来变成了工厂制造。

normal.en: Keep industrial and industrious apart: industrial is about factories, industrious is about hard work. The same root took two roads.
normal.cn: 把 industrial 与 industrious 分清：前者关于工厂，后者关于勤奋。同一词根走了两条路。

normal.en: The family runs industry → industrial → industrialize → industrialization, one suffix at a time.
normal.cn: 这个词族沿 industry → industrial → industrialize → industrialization 展开，每次加一个后缀。

normal.en: A skyline of smokestacks and conveyor belts is an industrial skyline; the adjective paints the whole scene.
normal.cn: 由烟囱和传送带构成的天际线就是 industrial 天际线；这个形容词把整个场景涂上颜色。

normal.en: The industrial revolution is the phrase that turned the adjective into the name of an age.
normal.cn: industrial revolution 这一短语把这个形容词变成了一个时代的名称。

abstract.en: Think of a conveyor belt as the spine of a factory: whatever the belt touches becomes industrial.
abstract.cn: 把传送带想象成工厂的脊椎：传送带碰到什么，什么就变成工业的。

abstract.en: Think of two words leaving one root: industrious stays with the worker's sweat, industrial walks into the factory.
abstract.cn: 想象两个词从同一词根出发：industrious 留在工人的汗水里，industrial 走进工厂。

abstract.en: Think of a map coloured grey wherever chimneys stand; that grey is the adjective's territory.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，凡有烟囱处就涂成灰色；这片灰色就是该形容词的领地。

examples.en: The Ruhr became the industrial heart of Germany in the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 鲁尔区在 19 世纪成为德国的工业心脏。

examples.en: Industrial action halted production for two weeks.
examples.cn: 工业行动使生产停顿了两周。

examples.en: Industrial design favours clean lines and cheap materials.
examples.cn: 工业设计偏爱简洁线条与廉价材料。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: industry（工业）+ -al（表所属）→ industrial 工业的；同根 industrious 却是「勤劳的」——一个进工厂，一个留在人身上

root: 拉丁 industria「勤勉、活动」+ 拉丁形容词后缀 -alis（英语 -al）；industria 一般认为是 indu-（in）+ struere「建造」。同根词 industrious 保留「勤奋」义，industrial 则沿「制造业」义发展。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses spread outward from 'of industry': the inputs industry uses, the places and eras it dominates, the relations inside it, the policies about it, its shares, and finally its machine-made look.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从「工业的」向外铺开：工业使用的投入品、它主导的地点与时代、它内部的劳资关系、关于它的政策、它的股票，最后是它机器制造的观感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a conveyor belt that never stops, turning material into finished goods.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条不停运转、把材料变成成品的传送带。

branches.en: THE CORE RELATION: what belongs to industry, including the materials and processes industry uses.
branches.cn: 核心关系：从属于工业的事物，包括工业使用的材料与流程。

branches.en: PLACE, ERA, SECTOR: regions filled with industry, industrial civilization, and the industrial sector of an economy.
branches.cn: 地点、时代与部门：布满工业的地区、工业文明，以及经济中的工业部门。

branches.en: WORKPLACE AND POLICY: relations between employers and workers, and government policy toward industry.
branches.cn: 劳资与政策：雇主与工人之间的关系，以及政府对工业的政策。

branches.en: FINANCE: industrials are the shares of industrial companies, an ellipsis of 'industrial shares'.
branches.cn: 金融：industrials 指工业公司的股票，是 industrial shares 的省略。

branches.en: STYLE: bare, functional, machine-made design is called industrial by metaphor.
branches.cn: 风格：朴素、功能化、机器制造的设计被隐喻地称为工业风。

intro.en: Industrial is a single suffix added to a noun: industry + -al. The suffix is Latin -alis, the ordinary maker of 'belonging to' adjectives, also seen in natural, national, and cultural.
intro.cn: industrial 只是名词加一个后缀：industry + -al。该后缀是拉丁 -alis，是构成表示所属关系的形容词的常规手段，也见于 natural、national、cultural。

latinIntro.en: Latin industria 'diligence' yielded both the personal adjective industrius and, much later, the manufacturing noun industry. The root appears as industr-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 industria「勤勉」既产出了描述人的形容词 industrius，也在很久以后产出了表示制造业的名词 industry。词根以 industr- 形式出现。

items.meaningCN: 工业；行业；勤勉（经古法语来自拉丁 industria）
items.example: The car industry is the largest employer in the region.
items.exampleCN: 汽车工业是该地区最大的雇主。

items.meaningCN: 勤劳的；勤勉的（-ous 形容词后缀）
items.example: An industrious apprentice learns faster.
items.exampleCN: 勤奋的学徒学得更快。

items.meaningCN: 工业的（-al 拉丁形容词后缀）
items.example: Industrial output fell during the recession.
items.exampleCN: 经济衰退期间工业产出下降。

items.meaningCN: 使工业化（-ize 动词后缀）
items.example: The plan aimed to industrialize the interior.
items.exampleCN: 该计划旨在使内陆地区工业化。

items.example: Industrialization brought both wealth and smog.
items.exampleCN: 工业化既带来财富，也带来烟雾。

items.meaningCN: 工业化的（-ed 形容词后缀）
items.example: Industrialized economies usually have a larger service sector.
items.exampleCN: 工业化经济体通常拥有更庞大的服务业。

items.meaning: an owner or manager of large industry
items.example: The industrialist donated land for a school.
items.exampleCN: 这位工业家捐地建了一所学校。

items.meaning: a social order centred on large-scale industry
items.meaningCN: 工业主义（-ism 制度／学说名词）
items.example: Industrialism reshaped family life.
items.exampleCN: 工业主义重塑了家庭生活。

items.meaning: the decline of manufacturing in a region
items.example: Deindustrialization left empty factories along the canal.
items.exampleCN: 去工业化在运河边留下空置的工厂。

definition_zh: 工业；产业；行业；勤劳（古义）
definition_en: the making of goods in factories, and any branch of business taken as a whole
core_image: 山谷里三家工厂沿河排开，烟囱、铁路与工人宿舍连成一片
scene: 山谷里三家工厂沿着河排开，烟囱、铁路和工人宿舍连成一片。The chemical industry arrived in the valley when the railway did.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「以工厂生产为主的工业部门」（第 1 个义项：把原料加工成商品的工业整体）；句意为铁路通到山谷时，化学工业也到了这里。图中可辨识物件：厂房、烟囱、铁路线、工人宿舍。

pos.zh: 工业；产业（不可数或可数）
勤劳；勤勉（古旧义，不可数）

senses.title: Factory production as a system
senses.titleCN: 工业（以工厂生产为主的体系）
senses.definition: the organised making of goods by machines in factories
senses.definitionCN: 在工厂里用机器有组织地制造商品
senses.example: The chemical industry arrived in the valley when the railway did.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路通到山谷时，化学工业也到了这里。
senses.why: The modern sense grew out of an older word for diligent activity, and it names the whole system of such activity rather than one firm.
senses.whyCN: 现代义从一个表示「勤勉活动」的旧词生长出来，指这类活动的整套体系，而非单个企业。

senses.title: A branch of business
senses.definition: a particular field of commercial activity, such as tourism or banking
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定商业领域，如旅游业或银行业
senses.example: The tourism industry hires more staff each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业每年夏天雇用更多员工。
senses.why: Once the word meant organised activity in general, any organised field of business could be called an industry.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词泛指有组织的活动，任何有组织的商业领域都可以叫一个行业。

senses.title: Firms seen against government and universities
senses.titleCN: 产业界（与政府、学界相对）
senses.definition: the business world taken as one party in policy discussions
senses.definitionCN: 在政策讨论中被当作一方的企业界
senses.example: Universities and industry share the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 大学与产业界共用这个实验室。
senses.why: A field of firms is addressed as a single party in policy talk, so a mass of businesses takes the name of the activity.
senses.whyCN: 一个领域的众多企业在政策讨论中被当作单一一方来对话，因此这群企业便用了这项活动的名称。

senses.title: The companies of one field together
senses.definition: the firms of a field considered as a group that can agree on rules
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域的公司被当作可以商定规则的整体
senses.example: The industry agreed on a common safety code.
senses.exampleCN: 该行业商定了一套共同的安全守则。
senses.why: A field's firms act together often enough that the word can mean the group itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一领域的公司常常一起行动，因此这个词也可以指这个群体本身。

senses.title: Diligence, in older writing
senses.definition: steady hard work, the sense the word carried before machines
senses.definitionCN: 持续刻苦地工作，是机器时代之前该词的意思
senses.example: The old essay praises industry as the root of wealth.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇旧文称赞勤勉是财富的根源。
senses.why: The oldest English sense was a habit of hard work, and traces of it survive in the adjective for a diligent person.
senses.whyCN: 英语中最早的意思是刻苦工作的习惯，这层意思仍留在表示「勤劳的」形容词里。

senses.title: A sector in economic statistics
senses.definition: one of the broad divisions of an economy, such as primary or service activity
senses.definitionCN: 经济中的一大门类，如第一产业或服务业
senses.example: Primary industry gives way to services in the statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 在统计中，第一产业让位于服务业。
senses.why: Statistical classification needs named blocks, and the word supplies the name for each block.
senses.whyCN: 统计分类需要给每一块命名，这个词就提供这些名称。

senses.title: Heavy as opposed to light production
senses.definition: the part of manufacturing that handles large machinery, fuel or metal
senses.definitionCN: 制造业中处理大型机械、燃料或金属的部分
senses.example: Heavy industry needs far more power than this grid can carry.
senses.exampleCN: 重工业需要的电力远超这张电网所能承载。
senses.why: Within factory work, a division by weight of plant and material became a fixed pair of terms.
senses.whyCN: 在工厂生产内部，按设备与材料的轻重作出的划分，成了一套固定的对举说法。

senses.title: The level of activity, as measured
senses.titleCN: 产业活动水平（统计指标）
senses.definition: the volume of production, reported as a rising or falling figure
senses.definitionCN: 生产规模，作为上升或下降的数字发布
senses.example: Industry expanded for six quarters and then stalled.
senses.exampleCN: 产业活动连续六个季度扩张，随后停滞。
senses.why: Measured output takes the name of the activity, so a chart can show industry rising without naming a firm.
senses.whyCN: 被计量的产出沿用活动的名称，因此一张图可以显示产业上升，却不点出任何企业。

intro.en: Industry came through French from Latin industria 'diligence, activity'. How that Latin word was formed is disputed, and the factory sense is only eighteenth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语中表示「勤勉、活动」的名词。这个拉丁词如何构成存在争议，指工厂生产的那层意思要到十八世纪才有。年代均为约数。

items.en: Industria meant 'diligence, assiduous activity, something done with effort'. It described a habit of work, not a branch of trade.
items.cn: industria 意为「勤勉、刻苦的活动、费力做成之事」，描述的是工作习惯，而非商业门类。

items.en: One long-standing suggestion reads the word as a prefix meaning 'in' plus a verb meaning 'to build'. That is a hypothesis about its shape and has not been demonstrated, so source uncertain.
items.cn: 一种流传较久的说法把这个词读作意为「在内」的前缀加意为「建造」的动词。这只是关于其构形的假说，未获证实，故来源不确定。

items.en: French industrie carried the word into English in the fifteenth century, still meaning skill and diligence in a craft.
items.cn: 法语 industrie 在十五世纪把这个词带入英语，仍指技艺上的灵巧与勤勉。

items.en: In the eighteenth century the word moved from a personal habit to the organised making of goods, and then to whole branches of it.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个词从个人习惯转向有组织的商品制造，随后又转向各个制造门类。

items.en: Nineteenth-century writing fixed the modern sense: industry as the system of factories, power and mass output.
items.cn: 十九世纪的写作固定了现代义：工业即工厂、动力与大批量产出的体系。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root in other roles, where two of them are easily confused; group two holds nouns for branches of economic activity.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该拉丁词根的其他词类形式，其中两个极易混淆；第二组是表示经济活动门类的名词。

entries.definition: Relating to factories and mass production; it describes the system, not the effort of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 与工厂和大批量生产有关，描述体系，而非个人的努力。

entries.definition: Hard-working and diligent; it kept the oldest sense while the noun moved to factories.
entries.definitionCN: 指勤奋刻苦，保留了最古老的意思，而名词已转向工厂。

entries.definition: A person who owns or controls large manufacturing businesses.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有或掌控大型制造企业的人。

entries.definition: To build factory production in a place or an economy.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地或某经济体中建立工厂生产。

entries.definition: A named part of an economy; it is the statistical term, and industry is one of its members.
entries.definitionCN: 经济中被命名的一部分，是统计术语，工业只是其中一员。

entries.definition: The activity of making goods, narrower than industry because it excludes mining and power.
entries.definitionCN: 制造商品的活动，比工业窄，因不含采矿与电力。

entries.definition: Commercial activity or a single firm; it need not involve factories at all.
entries.definitionCN: 商业活动或单个企业，未必涉及工厂。

entries.definition: Trade and exchange, the part of business that moves goods rather than makes them.
entries.definitionCN: 指贸易与交换，是商业中搬运商品而非制造的那部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin noun meant diligence, and diligence organised became the factory system.
normal.cn: 拉丁名词本指勤勉，被组织起来的勤勉后来成了工厂体系。

normal.en: The family splits: one adjective points at factories, another at a hard-working person.
normal.cn: 同族词分成两支：一个形容词指向工厂，另一个指向勤奋的人。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: heavy industry, light industry, chemical industry, tourism industry.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：重工业、轻工业、化学工业、旅游业。

normal.en: The same noun can mean one trade, all its firms, or the measured level of activity.
normal.cn: 同一名词可以指一个行业、该行业的全部企业，或被计量的活动水平。

normal.en: The older sense survives in a single adjective, which is why the pair is so often confused.
normal.cn: 较古老的意思只留在一个形容词里，这就是那一对词常被混淆的原因。

abstract.en: Picture three chimneys along a river and one railway line joining them.
abstract.cn: 想象河边的三根烟囱，由一条铁路连起来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that has worked all its life, and a shed built to replace it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只劳作一生的手，和一座为取代它而建的厂房。

abstract.en: Picture a chart rising while no single factory is named.
abstract.cn: 想象一张上升的图表，却不点出任何一家工厂。

examples.en: The government wants industry to use less coal.
examples.cn: 政府希望工业少用煤。

examples.en: The film industry employs more people than the shipyards.
examples.cn: 电影业雇用的人比造船厂多。

examples.en: He owed his fortune to industry rather than to luck.
examples.cn: 他的财富来自勤勉，而非运气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「indu（在内）+ stry（建造）」——在里面不停建造 → 勤勉 → 工业、行业

root: 拉丁语中表示「勤勉、活动」的名词经法语进入英语；其为「在内」前缀加「建造」动词的读法只是假说，未获证实，故来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one organised effort: diligence becomes factory production, that production becomes a trade, the trade becomes a party in policy, a group of firms, a statistical block, a weight class, and finally a line on a chart.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份被组织起来的努力展开：勤勉变成工厂生产，生产变成一个行业，行业变成政策中的一方、一群企业、统计上的一块、按轻重分的类别，最后变成图表上的一条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three factory chimneys along a river, joined by a rail line and surrounded by workers' housing.
core.cn: 核心意象：河边三根工厂烟囱，由铁路相连，周围是工人宿舍。

branches.en: THE FACTORY SYSTEM: general factory production and the heavy end of it are the same system at two weights.
branches.cn: 工厂体系：泛指工厂生产与其中的重工业，是同一体系的两个轻重档。

branches.en: ONE TRADE AND ITS FIRMS: a branch of business and the companies inside it are the same group seen as activity and as members.
branches.cn: 一个行业与其企业：商业门类与其中的公司，是同一群体被看作活动与成员。

branches.en: A PARTY IN POLICY: the business world speaks as one voice against government and universities.
branches.cn: 政策中的一方：企业界对政府与学界作为同一个声音说话。

branches.en: THE OLD HABIT: diligence is the personal virtue the word started from.
branches.cn: 古老的习惯：勤勉是这个词出发时的个人德性。

branches.en: THE STATISTICAL BLOCK: a sector in a table and a rising line on a chart are the same output counted twice.
branches.cn: 统计上的一块：表格中的部门与图表上上升的线，是同一产出被计了两次。

intro.en: Industry is a Latin noun of diligent activity taken into French and English; its family splits between the factory adjective and the diligent-person adjective.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示勤勉活动的拉丁名词，经法语进入英语；其词族分成「工厂的」与「勤劳的」两支形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin industria yields industrial, industrialize and industrialization, while the same stem also gives the adjective for a hard-working person.
latinIntro.cn: 这个拉丁名词衍生出工业的、使工业化与工业化等词；同一词干还给出表示勤奋的形容词。

items.example: The noun begins as a virtue, not a trade.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词起初是一种德性，而非行业。

items.example: The adjective describes the person the noun praised.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述名词所称赞的人。

items.example: French added the sense of a craft and then a trade.
items.exampleCN: 法语加进了「技艺」，再扩展到「行业」。

items.meaning: organised making; a branch of trade
items.meaningCN: 有组织的制造；商业门类
items.example: English kept both the old virtue and the new system.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留旧的德性与新的体系。

items.example: The suffix makes the factory adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示工厂的形容词。

items.example: The suffix makes the adjective for a diligent person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示勤劳的形容词。

items.example: The verb marks the change to factory production.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词标记转向工厂生产的变化。

items.example: The person suffix names the owner of large works.
items.exampleCN: 表示人的后缀指大型工厂的所有者。

items.example: The noun names the whole changeover.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指整场转变。

definition_zh: 不可避免的；必然发生的；必然的；不可避免的事
definition_en: certain to happen and impossible to avoid or prevent
core_image: 一条已经走到尽头的路：所有岔路都被封住，只剩这一个方向
scene: 赛场上，计时牌只剩最后几秒，对手的领先已无法追回。He accepted the inevitable defeat with a calm smile.
sceneCN: 这里 inevitable 是「不可避免的、必然发生的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：裁判看了看表并示意：还剩十秒、领先两球，结果现在已不可避免。图中可辨识物件：记分牌、裁判手表、球场、球员。

pos.zh: 不可避免的；必然发生的；意料之中的
必然发生的事（常用 the inevitable）

collocations.zh: 意料之中的事终于发生了

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Impossible to avoid
senses.definition: impossible to escape or prevent, no matter what one does
senses.definitionCN: 无论怎么做都无法逃脱或阻止
senses.example: With the road flooded, a delay was inevitable.
senses.exampleCN: 道路被淹，延误已无法避免。
senses.why: The word is the negation of evitable 'avoidable'. Latin evitabilis comes from evitare 'to shun'. To call something inevitable is to say that every route of avoidance is closed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 evitable“可避免的”的否定式。拉丁语 evitabilis 来自 evitare“躲避”。称某事 inevitable，就是说每一条躲避的路都已关闭。

senses.title: Certain to happen
senses.titleCN: 必然发生：时间到了就会来
senses.definition: sure to happen at some point, even if the exact time is unknown
senses.definitionCN: 在某个时点必定发生，即使具体时间未知
senses.example: Some conflict is inevitable when two teams share one budget.
senses.exampleCN: 两个团队共用一份预算时，某些冲突必然发生。
senses.why: Avoidance concerns a person's power; certainty concerns the event's arrival. The same word covers both because a thing that cannot be prevented is also a thing that will certainly come.
senses.whyCN: “躲避”关乎人有没有能力；“必然”关乎事件会不会到来。同一个词覆盖两者，因为无法被阻止的事，也就是必定会来的事。

senses.title: Logically necessary
senses.titleCN: 逻辑必然：由前提必然推出
senses.definition: following necessarily from the premises or the stated conditions
senses.definitionCN: 由前提或已陈述的条件必然推出
senses.example: If every voter must be counted, a recount is inevitable.
senses.exampleCN: 如果每一张选票都必须被计入，重新计票就是必然的。
senses.why: Logic turns the word from physical prevention to entailment: given the premises, no other conclusion can be drawn. This is necessity in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把这个词从“物理上阻止”转为“蕴含”：给定前提，就得不出别的结论。这是严格意义上的必然性。

senses.title: Predictable and routine
senses.titleCN: 意料之中：老一套、不出所料
senses.definition: so habitual or expected that it can be predicted with confidence
senses.definitionCN: 如此习惯或可预期，以至于能很有把握地预测
senses.example: The inevitable question came: who will pay for it?
senses.exampleCN: 那个意料之中的问题来了：谁来付钱？
senses.why: Here necessity is weakened into habit. The event is not logically forced, but experience makes it feel as if it could not be otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 这里“必然”被弱化成习惯。事件并非逻辑上被迫发生，但经验让它感觉仿佛不可能有别的样子。

senses.title: An unavoidable event (noun)
senses.definition: as a noun, an event or outcome that cannot be avoided
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时，指无法避免的事件或结果
senses.example: They prepared for the inevitable rather than pretending it would not come.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为不可避免的事做准备，而不是假装它不会来。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun by 1850. English often turns an adjective into a name for the thing that carries the quality, so 'the inevitable' is 'that which is inevitable'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在 1850 年前已可作名词。英语常把形容词变成具有该性质之物的名称，因此 the inevitable 就是“那个不可避免的东西”。

senses.title: Death, as the inevitable
senses.titleCN: 委婉语：死亡这一必然结局
senses.definition: in euphemistic usage, death, viewed as the one event no one escapes
senses.definitionCN: 委婉用法中指死亡，被视为无人能逃脱的那件事
senses.example: When the inevitable finally came, the family was ready.
senses.exampleCN: 当那不可避免的结局终于到来时，家人已经做好了准备。
senses.why: The noun use allows speakers to avoid the word death. The euphemism works because the adjective already says everything: it cannot be avoided, so it need not be named.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法让说话者避开“死亡”一词。这个委婉语之所以成立，是因为形容词已经说尽了一切：它无法避免，因此不必点名。

senses.title: Philosophically unchangeable
senses.titleCN: 哲学意义上的不可更改
senses.definition: in philosophy, describing what cannot be otherwise, especially under determinism or fate
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中描述不可能另有状态的事，尤在决定论或宿命论语境下
senses.example: The argument claims that every choice is inevitable in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 该论证声称，每一个选择事先都是必然的。
senses.why: Philosophy pushes the word to its limit: not merely unpreventable by us, but fixed in the structure of causes. Here inevitable approaches 'fated'.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把这个词推到极限：不只是我们无法阻止，而是在因果结构中被固定。此处 inevitable 接近“命中注定”。

senses.title: Unavoidably accompanying something
senses.titleCN: 必然伴随：代价无法剥离
senses.definition: always present as a cost or side effect of a chosen course
senses.definitionCN: 作为某项选择过程的代价或副作用而始终存在
senses.example: Some noise is inevitable in any city-centre flat.
senses.exampleCN: 任何市中心的公寓都不可避免地会有一些噪音。
senses.why: The word can attach to a drawback rather than an event: if you take the benefit, the accompanying cost cannot be separated from it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以附着在缺点而非事件上：如果你要那份好处，伴随的代价就无法从中剥离。

intro.en: Inevitable is a Latin negative built on evitare 'to avoid'. Its first English uses were about unavoidable outcomes; the noun and the death euphemism are 19c developments. The deepest origin of vitare is uncertain.
intro.cn: inevitable 是建立在 evitare“避开”之上的拉丁否定式。它最早的英语用法指无法避免的结果；名词用法与指死亡的委婉语是 19 世纪的发展。vitare 的更早来源并不确定。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'unavoidable, that cannot be evaded'. The earliest context is general predication, not yet a fixed noun.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“无法避免、无法躲开的”。最早的语境是一般性陈述，尚未固定为名词。

items.en: Inevitabilis is in- 'not' + evitabilis 'avoidable'. The prefix is privative: it denies the ability named by the adjective.
items.cn: inevitabilis 是 in-“不”+ evitabilis“可避免的”。这个前缀是否定性的：它否定形容词所指的能力。

items.en: Evitare 'to shun, avoid' is ex- 'out of' + vitare 'shun'. The ex- marks moving out of the way; the whole verb pictures stepping aside from something.
items.cn: evitare“躲避、避开”是 ex-“离开”+ vitare“躲避”。ex- 表示移出原来的路径；整个动词描绘的正是从某物旁边让开。

items.en: The further origin of vitare is uncertain. Standard etymological references treat it as unclear; older guesses linking it to via 'way' or to a root meaning 'away' are not established. Marked source uncertain.
items.cn: vitare 的更早来源不确定。通行词源资料将其视为不清楚；把它联系到 via“道路”或某个意为“离开”的词根的旧猜测并未得到确认。故标为来源不确定。

items.en: The noun use 'an inevitable thing' is recorded by 1850. English can nominalize the adjective with the definite article: the inevitable.
items.cn: 名词用法“不可避免之事”在 1850 年前已有记录。英语可用定冠词把形容词名词化：the inevitable。

items.en: The inevitable becomes a euphemism for death, and inevitability a key term in philosophy and in narratives of history. Inevitably spreads as the everyday adverb.
items.cn: the inevitable 成为指死亡的委婉语，inevitability 成为哲学与历史叙事中的关键术语。inevitably 则作为日常副词广泛使用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the evit- root; the near-meaning group separates 'cannot be avoided' from 'certain' and 'fated'.
note.cn: 形近组共享 evit- 词根；近义组区分“无法避免”“确定”与“命中注定”。

entries.definition: avoidable. It is rare but shows the positive form that inevitable negates.
entries.definitionCN: 可避免的。它虽少见，却显出被 inevitable 否定的肯定形式。

entries.definition: in a way that cannot be avoided; necessarily.
entries.definitionCN: 不可避免地；必然地。

entries.definition: the quality or state of being impossible to avoid.
entries.definitionCN: 必然性；不可避免的性质或状态。

entries.definition: impossible to avoid. It says the same thing with a native prefix and is less formal than inevitable.
entries.definitionCN: 无法避免的。它用本族语前缀表达同一意思，比 inevitable 更不正式。

entries.definition: impossible to escape or evade. It stresses being trapped rather than the certainty of an event.
entries.definitionCN: 无法逃脱的。它强调被困住，而不是事件本身的确定性。

entries.definition: sure to happen. It states confidence; inevitable adds that no prevention is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 确定的；必定发生的。它陈述把握；inevitable 另加“无法阻止”之意。

entries.definition: fixed by fate or destiny. It is mythological or literary, while inevitable can be purely logical.
entries.definitionCN: 由命运注定的。它带神话或文学色彩，而 inevitable 可以纯粹是逻辑的。

normalIntro.en: Real prefixes and real contrasts; in- here is 'not', and evitable is the positive word being denied.
normalIntro.cn: 真实前缀与真实对比；这里的 in- 是“不”，evitable 是被否定的肯定词。

normal.en: in- 'not' + evitable 'avoidable': inevitable is simply the denial of avoidability.
normal.cn: in-“不”+ evitable“可避免的”：inevitable 就是否定“可避免性”。

normal.en: Evitare contains vitare 'shun', not vita 'life'; the word has nothing to do with life.
normal.cn: evitare 含 vitare“躲避”，不是 vita“生命”；这个词与“生命”无关。

normal.en: Compare evitable, inevitably and inevitability: one root, one negative prefix, three parts of speech.
normal.cn: 对比 evitable、inevitably、inevitability：一个词根、一个否定前缀、三种词性。

normal.en: -able means 'can be': evitable = can be avoided; inevitable = cannot be avoided.
normal.cn: -able 意为“能被”：evitable＝能被避免；inevitable＝不能被避免。

normal.en: The noun the inevitable often means death, because death is the event no one avoids.
normal.cn: 名词 the inevitable 常指死亡，因为死亡是无人能避开的事件。

abstract.en: Picture doors closing one by one until only one remains open.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇扇门依次关上，最后只剩一扇还开着。

abstract.en: An equation whose result was fixed before you began solving.
abstract.cn: 一道在你开始求解之前结果就已固定的方程。

abstract.en: The future as a corridor whose side doors have already been sealed.
abstract.cn: 未来是一条走廊，两侧的门早已被封死。

examples.en: Given the shortage of staff, some delays are inevitable.
examples.cn: 鉴于人手短缺，一些延误是不可避免的。

examples.en: The committee treated the merger as inevitable and stopped debating it.
examples.cn: 委员会把合并视为必然，便停止了争论。

examples.en: Inevitably, the cheapest option failed first.
examples.cn: 不可避免地，最便宜的方案最先失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因爱我·逃不脱”——因为爱，我逃不脱，结局不可避免 → inevitable 不可避免的

root: 源自拉丁语 inevitabilis“无法避免的”，由 in-“不”+ evitabilis“可避免的”构成；evitabilis 来自 evitare“避开”，由 ex-“出、离开”+ vitare“躲避”构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of inevitable, all built on one closed route. The closure may be physical, logical, habitual, philosophical, or the final closure of death.
sensesIntro.cn: inevitable 的八个义项都建立在“一条被封闭的路”上。这种封闭可以是物理的、逻辑的、习惯性的、哲学性的，也可以是死亡那最后的封闭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every side road is closed, so only one direction remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：每条岔路都被封住，只剩一个方向。

branches.en: NO ESCAPE AND CERTAINTY: what cannot be prevented is also what will surely arrive.
branches.cn: 无路可躲与确定：无法被阻止的事，也必定会到来。

branches.en: NECESSITY: premises force a conclusion; a causal system leaves no alternative.
branches.cn: 必然性：前提迫使结论成立；因果系统不留别的可能。

branches.en: HABIT: experience makes an outcome feel fixed before it happens.
branches.cn: 习惯：经验让某个结果在发生前就显得已经固定。

branches.en: THE THING ITSELF: an unavoidable event, or a cost that cannot be separated from a benefit.
branches.cn: 事物本身：一个无法避免的事件，或无法与好处剥离的代价。

branches.en: DEATH: the one appointment no diplomacy can cancel.
branches.cn: 死亡：唯一无法通过任何周旋取消的约定。

intro.en: Inevitable is in- 'not' + evitabilis 'avoidable', from evitare 'avoid'. English adds -ably, -ability, -ableness, and keeps the rare positive evitable.
intro.cn: inevitable 是 in-“不”+ evitabilis“可避免的”，后者来自 evitare“避开”。英语加 -ably、-ability、-ableness，并保留少见的肯定形式 evitable。

latinIntro.en: Latin evitare 'shun, avoid' (ex- + vitare) and evitabilis 'avoidable'. Note that vitare is not vita 'life', though the forms look close.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 evitare“躲避、避开”（ex- + vitare）与 evitabilis“可避免的”。注意 vitare 不是 vita“生命”，尽管词形相近。

items.meaning: in a way that cannot be avoided; necessarily
items.example: Inevitably, the news spread faster than the official statement.
items.exampleCN: 不可避免地，消息比官方声明传得更快。

items.meaning: the quality of being impossible to avoid
items.meaningCN: 必然性；不可避免的性质
items.example: The report questions the inevitability of the collapse.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告质疑崩溃的必然性。

items.meaning: the state of being unavoidable (less common)
items.meaningCN: 不可避免的状态（较少用）
items.example: The inevitableness of the change silenced the room.
items.exampleCN: 变革的不可避免让全场沉默。

items.meaningCN: 可避免的；能够被躲开的
items.example: The loss was evitable, but no one acted in time.
items.exampleCN: 这次损失本可避免，但没人及时行动。

items.meaning: in a way that can be avoided (rare)
items.example: Such errors are evitably caused by haste.
items.exampleCN: 这类错误是可以通过不急躁而避免的。

items.example: Philosophers still debate the evitability of the outcome.
items.exampleCN: 哲学家仍在争论这一结果是否可避免。

items.meaning: impossible to avoid; a native-prefix parallel to inevitable
items.meaningCN: 无法避免的；用本族语前缀构成的同义平行形式
items.example: The overlap in duties was unavoidable.
items.exampleCN: 职责上的重叠无法避免。

items.meaning: in a way that cannot be avoided
items.example: The meeting unavoidably ran into lunchtime.
items.exampleCN: 会议不可避免地拖到了午饭时间。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 可避免的；能够被躲开的
躲避；避开（更早来源不确定）

definition_zh: 不可避免地；必然地；势必；无法阻止地
definition_en: in a way that cannot be avoided or prevented
core_image: 一块裂开的石碑，裂缝从顶端一路向下延伸，无法停住
scene: 仓库里的货架只用几根细木条支撑，管理员在巡检记录里写下判断。With such thin supports, the shelf will inevitably give way under the weight.
sceneCN: 这里指人力无法阻止的结局（第 2 个义项：无法阻止地）；句意为支撑太细，这个货架在重压下必然垮掉。

pos.zh: 不可避免地；必然地；势必

derivatives.zh: 不可避免的；必然发生的
不可避免的性质（较少用）

senses.title: The announced certainty
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to present a result as the predictable outcome of what came before
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，把随后的结果说成前情注定会带来的结局
senses.example: Inevitably, the discussion drifted back to the same old argument.
senses.exampleCN: 讨论不可避免地又绕回那个老话题。
senses.why: As a sentence adverb it colours the whole clause rather than one verb, telling the reader that the outcome was already settled.
senses.whyCN: 作为句子副词，它修饰整个小句而不是单个动词，向读者暗示结局早已注定。

senses.title: No one can stop it
senses.definition: in a way that cannot be prevented by any person or effort
senses.definitionCN: 以任何人都无法阻止的方式
senses.example: With such thin supports, the shelf will inevitably give way under the weight.
senses.exampleCN: 支撑太细，这个货架在重压下必然会垮。
senses.why: Placed before the verb, it claims practical impossibility rather than mere probability.
senses.whyCN: 放在动词前时，它说的是现实中办不到，而不只是可能性很大。

senses.title: Logical consequence
senses.definition: as a conclusion that must follow from the stated premises
senses.definitionCN: 作为由既定前提必然推出的结论
senses.example: If every premise is true, the conclusion follows inevitably.
senses.exampleCN: 如果每个前提都成立，结论就必然随之而来。
senses.why: In logic the word marks deductive necessity, a stronger claim than empirical likelihood.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑语境中它标记演绎必然性，比经验上的可能性更强。

senses.title: Not necessarily
senses.definition: used with a negative to deny that one thing must lead to another
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，否认一件事必定引出另一件事
senses.example: A wealthy country is not inevitably a peaceful one.
senses.exampleCN: 富裕的国家未必就是和平的国家。
senses.why: Under negation the word stops asserting necessity; the sentence says the link is avoidable, not that it never occurs.
senses.whyCN: 在否定句中它不再断言必然，句子说的是这条联系可以避免，而不是从不发生。

senses.title: As always happens
senses.definition: used of a repeated event that experience makes predictable
senses.definitionCN: 用于经验上早已可料的重复事件
senses.example: As inevitably happens at long meetings, someone raised the coffee question.
senses.exampleCN: 正如长会上一贯会发生的那样，有人提起了咖啡的问题。
senses.why: The habitual frame turns inevitability into a comment on human routine, often with a touch of resignation.
senses.whyCN: 习惯性框架把必然转成对人世间惯例的评注，常带一点无奈。

senses.title: Coupled with something
senses.definition: used before a past participle to say that two things always come together
senses.definitionCN: 放在过去分词前，表示两件事总是同时出现
senses.example: Rapid expansion is inevitably accompanied by administrative strain.
senses.exampleCN: 快速扩张必然伴随行政上的紧绷。
senses.why: Here it modifies a participle rather than a finite verb, describing an inseparable pairing rather than one future event.
senses.whyCN: 这里修饰分词而非限定动词，描述的是不可分离的伴随关系，而不是某一件将来的事。

senses.title: The formal claim of a law
senses.definition: in academic or formal prose, used to present a general rule as beyond exception
senses.definitionCN: 在学术或正式散文中，把一般规律说成没有例外
senses.example: Any measure of this kind inevitably raises questions about privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这类措施必然引发关于隐私的疑问。
senses.why: The formal register uses the adverb as a rhetorical seal, claiming a general law rather than predicting one case.
senses.whyCN: 正式语域把它当作修辞上的封印，声称的是一条普遍规律，而不是预测某一次情形。

senses.title: Unavoidably incurred
senses.titleCN: 过程中无法免除的代价
senses.definition: used of costs or losses that must be accepted in a process
senses.definitionCN: 用于某个过程中必须承受的成本或损耗
senses.example: Some loss of detail is inevitably incurred when a file is compressed.
senses.exampleCN: 压缩文件时，细节的损失是无法免除的。
senses.why: Technical writing uses the word for unavoidable by-products of a procedure, where no agent is to blame.
senses.whyCN: 技术写作里它指程序中无法避免的副产物，并不归咎于某个人。

intro.en: Inevitably comes from the Latin adjective for unavoidable plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词的直接来源很清楚：拉丁语「不可回避的」形容词加英语副词后缀。只有英语首见年代是约数，不构成来源争议。

items.en: The verb vitare means to shun or avoid, and it supplies the core of the later adjective.
items.cn: 动词意为「躲开、回避」，为后来的形容词提供词干。

items.en: The prefix e-, meaning out, plus vitare forms evitabilis, that which can be avoided.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的前缀与「回避」合成「可以躲开的」。

items.en: The negating prefix in- turns evitabilis into inevitabilis, that which cannot be avoided.
items.cn: 否定前缀加在「可以躲开的」上，得到「躲不开的」。

items.en: French inévitable and English inevitable carry the adjective into general use; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 法语与英语的形容词把这一说法带入通用语；英语首见年代只是约数。

items.en: English adds its adverb suffix to the adjective, and the new form takes over the sentence-initial role.
items.cn: 英语在形容词上加副词后缀，这个新形式随后承担句首评注功能。

items.en: Modern usage spreads from fatalistic speech to technical and academic claims of necessity.
items.cn: 现代用法从宿命式口语扩展到技术与学术上的必然性断言。

note.en: The first group belongs to the same Latin avoid-root family; the second group names ways of saying that something cannot be escaped.
note.cn: 第一组同属拉丁语「回避」词族；第二组是表达「逃不掉」的近义说法。

entries.definition: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 必定发生且无法避免的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The quality of being impossible to avoid.
entries.definitionCN: 无法避免的性质；必然性。

entries.definition: Able to be avoided; rare, and formed without the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 可避免的；较少见，未带否定前缀。

entries.definition: The state of being unavoidable, a rarer noun than inevitability.
entries.definitionCN: 不可避免的状态，比必然性一词更少用。

entries.definition: As a logical or causal result that cannot be otherwise.
entries.definitionCN: 作为无法另作他解的逻辑或因果结果。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be avoided in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 在实际中无法避开地。

entries.definition: As an immediate result, without a separate decision or effort.
entries.definitionCN: 作为直接结果自动发生，无需另作决定或努力。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be escaped or resisted; literary and formal.
entries.definitionCN: 无法逃脱或抗拒地；书面而正式。

entries.definition: Because circumstances leave no other choice.
entries.definitionCN: 因情形所迫而没有别的选择。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real negative prefix, the real avoid-root and the real sentence patterns.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的否定前缀、真实的「回避」词根与真实句式。

normal.en: The prefix means not and the root means avoid, so the word is simply cannot be avoided.
normal.cn: 前缀表示「不」，词根表示「避开」，合起来就是「躲不开」。

normal.en: Rain does not ask permission before falling, and that is the tone of this word.
normal.cn: 雨点落下前不会征求同意，这正是这个词的语气。

normal.en: Put it first in a sentence and the comma falls like a judge's gavel.
normal.cn: 把它放在句首，后面的逗号就像法槌落下。

normal.en: Under negation it retreats at once: not inevitable means only not necessarily.
normal.cn: 在否定句里它立刻退让：不是必然，只是未必。

normal.en: Engineering reports like it for costs that no procedure can remove.
normal.cn: 工程报告爱用它给无法免除的损耗定性。

abstract.en: Inevitability is not a prediction of a date but an admission that the end was written into the conditions.
abstract.cn: 必然不是预言某一天，而是承认结局早已写在条件里。

abstract.en: The feeling of inevitability comes from looking back, when every step seems to have had no alternative.
abstract.cn: 真正的必然感来自回头看，那时每一步都像没得选。

abstract.en: The adverb quietly moves responsibility away from people and onto the nature of things.
abstract.cn: 这个副词把责任从人身上悄悄拿走，交给事情本身。

examples.en: Inevitably, the first draft raised more questions than it answered.
examples.cn: 初稿不可避免地提出的问题多于它回答的问题。

examples.en: Without maintenance, the pipes will inevitably corrode.

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate sentence-level fatalism, practical impossibility, deductive necessity, negated necessity, habitual resignation, inseparable pairing, formal law-claims and unavoidable process costs.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cracked stone tablet whose fracture runs from top to bottom and cannot be halted.

branches.en: THE ANNOUNCED OUTCOME: the sentence adverb that declares a result settled.

branches.en: THE BLOCKED PATH: no person or effort can prevent it.
branches.cn: 被堵死的路：任何人、任何努力都挡不住。

branches.en: THE LAW-LIKE CLAIM: deductive necessity and the formal assertion of a general rule.
branches.cn: 近乎规律的断言：演绎必然后承与书面语中的一般规律。

branches.en: THE DENIED LINK: under negation the word means not necessarily.
branches.cn: 被否认的链条：在否定句中意为「未必」。

branches.en: THE ACCEPTED PRICE: habit, inseparable pairing and costs incurred by a process.
branches.cn: 接受的代价：习惯性重演、如影随形的伴随，以及过程无法免除的损耗。

intro.en: Inevitably is built from a Latin negative prefix, a Latin avoid-root, two Latin suffixes and an English adverb suffix; every part is transparent.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语否定前缀、「回避」词根、两个拉丁后缀与一个英语副词后缀构成，每个构件都清楚可辨。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family starts from the verb for shun and builds an adjective of possibility, which the negative prefix then reverses.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族从表示「回避」的动词出发，先构成表可能性的形容词，再由否定前缀把它反转。

items.example: The prefix reverses the possibility carried by the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀把形容词所表的可能性反转过来。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of getting out of the way.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「让开、脱身」的意思。

items.example: The verb supplies the physical image of stepping aside.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「侧身避开」的具体意象。

items.example: The prefixed verb strengthens the act of avoidance.
items.exampleCN: 加前缀的动词强化了「避开」这一动作。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into a statement about possibility.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成关于可能性的说法。

items.example: The adjective is the positive base that the negative prefix later blocks.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是肯定基形，随后被否定前缀挡住。

items.example: The negated adjective passes through French into English.
items.exampleCN: 带否定的形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成方式副词。

items.example: The noun names the quality that the adverb asserts.

senses.definition: a very young child who cannot yet walk or talk

senses.example: The infant slept quietly in her mother's arms.

items.en: From Latin infans, meaning unable to speak, formed from in- (not) plus the root of fari (to speak).
items.cn: 源自拉丁语 infans，意为「不会说话的」，由 in-（不）加 fari（说话）的词根构成。

items.cn: 在晚期拉丁语中，infans 已转为名词，指很小的孩子。

items.en: Old French borrowed the word as enfant, keeping both the noun and adjective senses.
items.cn: 古法语将其借入为 enfant，同时保留名词与形容词两种用法。

items.en: English took the word from French in the fourteenth century, first as a young person and soon as a baby.
items.cn: 英语于十四世纪经由法语引入该词，最初泛指年轻人，很快专指婴儿。

items.en: The adjective senses for early stages of businesses and skills developed by extension in later centuries.
