definition_zh: 感染；传染；传染病；感染部位；（计算机）感染
definition_en: the entry and growth of a germ inside the body, or a disease caused by such a germ
core_image: 一群微小的病原穿过伤口，进入身体并开始繁殖
scene: 厨房里，有人划伤了手指却没清洗包扎，伤口渐渐红肿。The wound became red and swollen because an infection had set in.
sceneCN: 这里 infection 指「感染」（第 1 个义项：病原进入体内并繁殖的过程）；句意：伤口变得红肿，因为感染已经发生。图中可辨识物件：伤口、红肿皮肤、病原颗粒、白细胞。

pos.zh: 感染；传染；传染病；感染部位；（计算机）病毒感染；思想的感染（比喻）

senses.title: Invasion by a germ
senses.titleCN: 感染：病原进入体内并繁殖的过程
senses.definition: the process by which a germ enters the body, settles in a tissue and multiplies there
senses.definitionCN: 病原进入身体、定位于某一组织并在其中繁殖的过程
senses.example: The wound became red and swollen because an infection had set in.
senses.exampleCN: 伤口变得红肿，因为感染已经发生。
senses.why: Latin inficere meant 'to put into, to dye', and the medical sense keeps that picture: something is put into the body and spreads through it like dye through cloth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 inficere 意为「放入、染色」，医学义保留了这幅画面：某物被放进身体，像染料浸透布一样在其中扩散。

senses.title: A disease so caused
senses.titleCN: 传染病：由病原引起的一种疾病
senses.definition: a disease caused by a germ, especially one that can be treated or must be reported
senses.definitionCN: 由病原引起的疾病，尤指需要治疗或必须上报的疾病
senses.example: She missed two weeks of school with a chest infection.
senses.exampleCN: 她因胸部感染缺课两周。
senses.why: English uses the process word for the illness itself because the cause and the condition are hard to separate in ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 英语用表示过程的词来指疾病本身，因为在日常语言中病因与病况很难分开。

senses.title: Transmission event
senses.titleCN: 传染：病原从一个人传到另一个人的事件
senses.definition: the passing of a germ from one person, animal or surface to another
senses.definitionCN: 病原从一个人、动物或物体表面传到另一处的过程
senses.example: The infection spread through the ward within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 感染在一周内传遍了整个病房。
senses.why: Spread is the most visible part of the process, so the same noun names the event of passing on as well as the state of being invaded.
senses.whyCN: 扩散是这一过程最可见的部分，因此同一个名词既指被侵入的状态，也指传播这一事件。

senses.title: A localised site
senses.titleCN: 感染灶：局限在某一部位的感染
senses.definition: a confined infection in one place, such as a wound, the bladder or a joint
senses.definitionCN: 局限于某一处的感染，如伤口、膀胱或关节
senses.example: The doctor drained the infection in his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把他膝部的感染引流了。
senses.why: Once a site can be examined and drained, the abstract process becomes a countable object, and clinicians speak of 'an infection' in a place.
senses.whyCN: 当一个部位可以被检查与引流，抽象过程就变成了可数对象，临床医生便说「某处有一个感染」。

senses.title: Systemic infection
senses.titleCN: 全身性感染：病原或其产物进入血液
senses.definition: an infection that has spread beyond its starting point into the blood or the whole body
senses.definitionCN: 已超出起始部位、进入血液或波及全身的感染
senses.example: A local infection can become systemic if it is left untreated.
senses.exampleCN: 局部感染若不治疗，可能变成全身性感染。
senses.why: The body is treated as a space with a boundary; when the germ crosses that boundary, the same word gains a severity it did not have before.
senses.whyCN: 身体被看作一个有边界的空间；当病原越过这个边界，同一个词就获得了此前没有的严重程度。

senses.title: Hospital-acquired infection
senses.titleCN: 医院获得性感染：住院期间新发生的感染
senses.definition: an infection a patient acquires during medical care that was not present on arrival
senses.definitionCN: 患者在接受医疗期间新获得、入院时并不存在的感染
senses.example: Hand washing sharply reduced hospital-acquired infections.
senses.exampleCN: 勤洗手大幅减少了医院获得性感染。
senses.why: Hospitals concentrate sick people and invasive devices, so transmission there became a distinct problem with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 医院集中了病人与侵入性器械，因此那里的传播成了有专名的独立问题。

senses.title: Computer infection
senses.titleCN: 计算机感染：恶意程序潜入系统并扩散
senses.definition: the entry and spread of malicious software in a computer system, named by analogy with disease
senses.definitionCN: 恶意软件进入计算机系统并扩散，借用疾病传播的比喻命名
senses.example: The lab lost a week of data to a computer infection.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室因一次计算机感染损失了一周的数据。
senses.why: A program that copies itself inside a host and spreads to others behaves like a germ, so the medical vocabulary was borrowed wholesale.
senses.whyCN: 一个在宿主内自我复制并传给其他系统的程序，行为像病原，于是医学术语被整套借走。

senses.title: Contagion of ideas
senses.titleCN: 思想的感染：观念、情绪在人群中蔓延
senses.definition: the spread of an idea, a mood or a habit through a group, pictured as a disease passing between people
senses.definitionCN: 观念、情绪或习惯在群体中扩散，被想象为疾病在人际间传递
senses.example: Panic is an infection that travels faster than any virus.
senses.exampleCN: 恐慌是一种传播得比任何病毒都快的感染。
senses.why: The metaphor works because both germs and ideas need carriers and both spread faster in close contact, so 'infection' became a word for social contagion.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，是因为病原与观念都需要载体，且都在密切接触中传得更快，于是 infection 成了社会性传染的词。

intro.en: Infection comes from Latin infectio, a dyeing or staining, from inficere 'to put into, to dip, to taint'. The modern medical sense grew out of the idea of a body being stained from within.
intro.cn: infection 来自拉丁 infectio「染色、污染」，源于 inficere「放入、浸入、使染污」。现代医学义正是从「身体从内部被染污」这一意象生长出来的。

items.en: Facere meant 'to make, to do, to put'; it is the verb behind factory, effect and defect, and its past participle factus shaped a large family.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造、放置」；它是 factory、effect、defect 背后的动词，其过去分词 factus 塑造了一个庞大的词族。

items.en: In- 'into' plus facere gave inficere, literally 'to put into'. It was used for dipping cloth into dye, and from that for staining, tainting and poisoning.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 facere 得 inficere，字面即「放入」。它用于把布浸入染料，由此引申为染色、污染、下毒。

items.en: The noun infectio named the act of dyeing or staining, and by extension a taint or contamination, including contamination of the body.
items.cn: 名词 infectio 指染色或污染的动作，并引申为沾染、污损，包括身体受到污染。

items.en: English infection appears in the fourteenth century; plague writing of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries made it a common word for a disease passed between people.
items.cn: 英语 infection 出现于 14 世纪；16、17 世纪的瘟疫文献使它成为指人际传播疾病的常用词。

items.en: In the nineteenth century, when specific microbes were shown to cause specific diseases, infection was fixed to the entry and growth of those organisms.
items.cn: 19 世纪，当特定微生物被证明引起特定疾病后，infection 被固定为这些生物进入并繁殖的过程。

items.en: Twentieth-century computing and social writing extended the word to malicious code and to the spread of ideas, both still felt as metaphors.
items.cn: 20 世纪的计算机与社会写作把这个词扩展到恶意代码与观念传播，两者至今仍被感觉是比喻。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same Latin verb or differing only in ending; the second holds medical and figurative terms that overlap with infection.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在同一拉丁动词上、或只差词尾的词；第二组是与 infection 语义重叠的医学与比喻术语。

entries.definition: To give a germ to someone or something; infection is the process or the resulting state.
entries.definitionCN: 把病原传给某人或某物；infection 是过程或由此形成的状态。

entries.definition: Able to be passed on to others; it describes a disease or a person, not the invasion itself.
entries.definitionCN: 能够传给他人；它描述疾病或人，而非侵入过程本身。

entries.definition: The presence of parasites such as lice or insects on a body or in a place; it is not a microbial infection.
entries.definitionCN: 虱、昆虫等较大寄生虫在身体或某处的存在；它不是微生物感染。

entries.definition: The body's reaction to injury or infection, marked by heat, pain and swelling; it can occur without a germ.
entries.definitionCN: 身体对损伤或感染的反应，表现为热、痛、肿；它可以没有病原而发生。

entries.definition: The passing of a disease by direct or indirect contact; infection is the broader term for invasion itself.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病经直接或间接接触传播；infection 是更宽泛的「侵入」术语。

entries.definition: An abnormal condition of the body with a definite set of signs; a disease may or may not be caused by infection.
entries.definitionCN: 具有一组明确体征的身体异常状态；疾病可能由感染引起，也可能不。

entries.definition: A life-threatening whole-body response to infection; it is the severe end of the infection spectrum.
entries.definitionCN: 对感染产生的危及生命的全身反应；它是感染谱系中最严重的一端。

entries.definition: The stable presence of germs on or in a body without invasion or symptoms; infection implies damage or response.
entries.definitionCN: 微生物在体表或体内稳定存在而无侵入或症状；infection 则意味着损害或反应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'into' + facere 'put' gives inficere 'put into', the literal origin of infection.
normal.cn: in-「进入」+ facere「放」得 inficere「放入」，这就是 infection 的字面来源。

normal.en: The family runs infect, infection, infectious, infected, infectivity, disinfect.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 infect、infection、infectious、infected、infectivity、disinfect。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the source: bacterial infection, viral infection, source of infection.
normal.cn: 固定搭配命名来源：细菌感染、病毒感染、传染源。

normal.en: infection is the noun, infect is the verb, infectious is the adjective: choose by grammar, not by sound.
normal.cn: infection 是名词，infect 是动词，infectious 是形容词：按语法而非读音选用。

normal.en: Same word, new hosts: computer infection and the infection of panic.
normal.cn: 同一个词，新的宿主：计算机感染与恐慌的感染。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of dye entering a cloth and slowly taking over the whole square.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴染料落进布中，慢慢占满整块方形。

abstract.en: Picture a small fire spreading along a floor that has not been cleaned.
abstract.cn: 想象一点火沿未清理的地面蔓延。

abstract.en: Picture a mood moving across a crowded room without anyone touching.
abstract.cn: 想象一种情绪穿过拥挤的房间，没有人接触却都染上了。

examples.en: Wash your hands to lower the risk of infection.
examples.cn: 洗手以降低感染风险。

examples.en: The infection responded quickly to antibiotics.
examples.cn: 感染对抗生素反应很快。

examples.en: The company called the leak an infection of its network.
examples.cn: 公司把这次泄露称为其网络的感染。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in 进入 + fect 做／放」——有东西被放进了身体并在里面繁殖 → infection 感染

root: 拉丁 in-「进入」+ facere「放；做」→ inficere「浸入、染污」→ infectio「染色；污染」→ 英语 infection（14 世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one entry: the germ entering and growing, the illness it causes, the passing from person to person, a confined site, a whole-body spread, a hospital form, a computer form, and finally an idea spreading like a mood.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次进入展开：病原进入并繁殖、由此引起的疾病、人际传播、局限的感染灶、全身扩散、医院内的形式、计算机形式，最后是像情绪一样扩散的观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: germs crossing a break in the skin and settling inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：病原越过皮肤的破口，落脚在身体内部。

branches.en: PROCESS AND RESULT: the invasion itself, then the disease it leaves behind.
branches.cn: 过程与结果：侵入本身，然后是它留下的疾病。

branches.en: BETWEEN PEOPLE: the same noun names the event of transmission.
branches.cn: 人与人之间：同一个名词也命名传播事件。

branches.en: FROM A POINT TO THE WHOLE: a wound or bladder can hold it, or it can enter the blood.
branches.cn: 从一点到全身：它可局限于伤口或膀胱，也可进入血液。

branches.en: THE HOSPITAL: crowded care creates its own pattern of spread.
branches.cn: 医院：密集的照护造出自身的传播模式。

branches.en: NEW HOSTS: code and ideas are infected in the same grammar as bodies.
branches.cn: 新的宿主：代码与观念用与身体相同的语法被「感染」。

intro.en: Infection is in- 'into' plus facere 'put' plus -tio, a noun of action; the same pieces build inflect and inject with different verbs.
intro.cn: infection 是 in-「进入」加 facere「放」再加 -tio（动作名词后缀）；同样的部件配不同动词还造出 inflect、inject。

latinIntro.en: Latin inficere, infectio and infectus supply the family; dis- and re- build disinfect and reinfect from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 inficere、infectio、infectus 提供词族；dis- 与 re- 在同一词干上造出 disinfect、reinfect。

definition_zh: 通货膨胀；充气；膨胀；夸大
definition_en: a sustained rise in the general level of prices, or the act of filling something with air and swelling it
core_image: 市场里的价签一个月换了两回，同样一袋钱能买到的面包越来越少
scene: 战后的集市上，面包的价签一个月换了两回，主妇把钱袋攥得更紧，摊主还在往上改数字。 Prices kept climbing, and the country was warned that inflation would reach double digits.
sceneCN: 这里 inflation 指「一般物价水平持续上涨」（第 1 个义项：整体物价持续上升、货币购买力随之下降）；句意为物价不断攀升，该国被警告通胀将达到两位数。图中可辨识物件：反复改写的价签、面包篮、钱袋、记账板。

pos.zh: 通货膨胀；充气；膨胀；夸大

senses.title: A sustained rise in the price level
senses.definition: a continuing increase in the general level of prices, so that money buys less over time
senses.definitionCN: 整体物价水平持续上升，使同样多的钱随时间买到的东西越来越少
senses.example: Prices kept climbing, and the country was warned that inflation would reach double digits.
senses.exampleCN: 物价不断攀升，该国被警告通胀将达到两位数。
senses.why: The image is a balloon being blown up: the stock of money or the level of prices swells, and the metaphor became the standard economic term in the nineteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 意象是被吹胀的气球：货币量或物价水平鼓起来，这个比喻在 19 世纪成了标准经济术语。

senses.title: The act of filling with air
senses.definition: the act of filling a tyre, balloon or other container with air or gas
senses.definitionCN: 往轮胎、气球或其他容器中注入空气或气体的动作
senses.example: Inflation of the raft took twenty minutes with a hand pump.
senses.exampleCN: 用手动气泵给救生筏充气花了二十分钟。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: the Latin verb meant to blow into something, and the noun simply names that action.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理义：拉丁动词意为「吹入某物」，名词只是给这个动作命名。

senses.title: The state of being swollen
senses.definition: the condition of something that has been blown up and now bulges or expands
senses.definitionCN: 某物被充气后鼓起或胀大的状态
senses.example: The doctor noted a slight inflation below the knee.
senses.exampleCN: 医生注意到膝盖下方有轻微肿胀。
senses.why: From the action the noun moves to its result, so inflation can name a bulge in a body or a material.
senses.whyCN: 名词从动作转向结果，因此 inflation 也能指身体或材料上的鼓包。

senses.title: Exaggeration in speech
senses.definition: a swelling of language in which praise, claims or promises are blown up beyond the facts
senses.definitionCN: 语言上的膨胀，即赞美、主张或承诺被吹到超出事实的程度
senses.example: The brochure's claims were pure inflation of a modest trial.
senses.exampleCN: 宣传册里的说法，只是把一次小规模试验大大吹胀。
senses.why: The same balloon image serves rhetoric: words are pumped up until they no longer match the thing described.
senses.whyCN: 同一个气球意象也服务于修辞：词被吹大，直到与所描述之物不再相称。

senses.title: The inflation rate
senses.definition: a percentage expressing the pace at which the general level of prices is rising
senses.definitionCN: 表示整体物价水平上涨速度的百分数
senses.example: The inflation rate fell to three percent after the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 秋收之后，通胀率降到百分之三。
senses.why: A process noun readily stands for its own measure, which is why the word can be placed directly before rate.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词很容易转指自身的度量，因此这个词可以直接放在 rate 之前。

senses.title: Demand-pull inflation
senses.definition: price rises caused by spending that outruns the supply of goods available
senses.definitionCN: 由支出超过现有商品供给所引起的物价上涨
senses.example: Demand-pull inflation showed up first in building materials.
senses.exampleCN: 需求拉动型通胀最先出现在建筑材料上。
senses.why: When buyers bid more than the stock can answer, the rise is traced to the demand side and named accordingly.
senses.whyCN: 当买方的出价超过存货所能应付的量，上涨就被追溯到需求一侧，并据此命名。

senses.title: Cost-push inflation
senses.definition: price rises caused by higher wages, energy or material costs being passed on to buyers
senses.definitionCN: 由工资、能源或材料成本上升并转嫁给买方所引起的物价上涨
senses.example: Cost-push inflation followed the doubling of fuel prices.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料价格翻倍之后，出现了成本推动型通胀。
senses.why: The same rise can be traced from the producer's costs rather than from the buyer's demand, giving the mirror term.
senses.whyCN: 同样的上涨也可以从生产者的成本而非买方的需求去追溯，于是有了这个镜像说法。

senses.title: Runaway hyperinflation
senses.definition: inflation that accelerates beyond control until the currency ceases to serve as a store of value
senses.definitionCN: 加速到无法控制、直至货币不再能保值的地步的通胀
senses.example: Hyperinflation ended with banknotes carried in wheelbarrows.
senses.exampleCN: 恶性通胀以用独轮车推钞票收场。
senses.why: At the extreme the balloon bursts, and a separate word takes over to mark that the ordinary measure has failed.
senses.whyCN: 到了极端，气球炸开，另有一个词接手，标记常规度量已经失效。

intro.en: Inflation comes from Latin inflatio 'a blowing into, a swelling', built on inflare 'to blow into', from in- 'in' and flare 'to blow'. The economic sense is nineteenth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: inflation 来自拉丁 inflatio「吹入、膨胀」，由 inflare「吹入」构成，即 in-「进入」加 flare「吹」。经济义是 19 世纪才有的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Flare meant 'to blow, to breathe out'; it is the source of several English words about blowing and breathing.
items.cn: flare 意为「吹、呼出气」；英语中若干与吹气、呼吸有关的词都源于它。

items.en: In- 'into' plus flare produced inflare 'to blow into, to puff up', used of breath, wind and swollen things.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 flare 构成 inflare「吹入、使鼓起」，用于气息、风与鼓胀之物。

items.en: The noun inflatio named both the act of blowing into something and the swelling that followed.
items.cn: 名词 inflatio 既指吹入某物的动作，也指随之而来的肿胀。

items.en: English inflation is recorded from the seventeenth century in medical and natural-philosophical writing for swelling and the filling of a space with air.
items.cn: 英语 inflation 自 17 世纪见于医学与自然哲学写作，指肿胀以及用空气充满某处。

items.en: The monetary use is generally dated to the nineteenth century, when an excessive issue of money was pictured as blowing the currency up like a balloon.
items.cn: 货币义一般认为是 19 世纪的产物，当时把过量发行货币想象成把通货像气球一样吹胀。

items.en: Source uncertain (first monetary citation): the metaphor is plain, but the earliest printed use in the price sense is disputed and may belong to a later decade, so no firm date is given here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（货币义的最早书证）：比喻本身清楚，但物价义最早的印刷用例有争议，可能晚数十年，此处不给出确定年代。

note.en: The first group holds the opposite process, the verb behind this noun, and one word that only looks similar; the second holds phrases for rising prices of different breadth.
note.cn: 第一组是相反的过程、本名词背后的动词，以及一个只是长得像的词；第二组是范围不同的「物价上涨」说法。

entries.definition: The mirror image: prices fall and the currency gains purchasing power instead of losing it.
entries.definitionCN: 镜像过程：物价下跌，货币购买力上升而非下降。

entries.definition: To fill with air or to push prices up; the noun inflation names the process or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 充气，或把价格推高；名词 inflation 指这个过程或其结果。

entries.definition: Describes forces or pressure that produce inflation; it does not name the rise itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述造成通胀的力量或压力；它不指上涨本身。

entries.definition: From Latin flectere 'to bend', not flare 'to blow': it means a bend in pitch or a change in word form, and is no relative.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 flectere「弯曲」，而非 flare「吹」：指语调的弯折或词形变化，并非同族。

entries.definition: An everyday phrase for higher prices; it can describe one item, while inflation implies the general level.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指价格上涨；可指单件商品，而 inflation 暗示整体水平。

entries.definition: Names the rise as households feel it through the basket of goods they buy.
entries.definitionCN: 从家庭角度命名上涨，即通过日常购买的一篮子商品感受到的涨价。

entries.definition: A general word for something intensifying; it carries no economic measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某事物加剧升级；不带经济度量含义。

entries.definition: Growth in size, volume or output; it can accompany inflation but does not mean it.
entries.definitionCN: 指尺寸、体积或产出的扩大；可与通胀同时发生，但并不等于通胀。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin root, a real family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'into' plus flare 'to blow': to blow into something until it swells.
normal.cn: in-「进入」加 flare「吹」：往某物里吹，直到它鼓起来。

normal.en: The family runs inflate, inflation, inflationary, inflator, deflate, deflation.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：inflate、inflation、inflationary、inflator、deflate、deflation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: inflation rate, double-digit inflation, curb inflation, inflation target.
normal.cn: 固定说法：通胀率、两位数通胀、抑制通胀、通胀目标。

normal.en: The balloon image survives: an over-issued currency is a balloon blown too full.
normal.cn: 气球意象仍在：超发的货币就是吹得太满的气球。

normal.en: Do not confuse the root with flectere 'to bend', which gives inflection.
normal.cn: 别把词根与 flectere「弯曲」混淆，后者给出 inflection。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag rewritten while the ink is still wet.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签，墨迹未干就被改写。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon that keeps filling until the skin is thin and shiny.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球不断充气，表皮变得又薄又亮。

abstract.en: Picture a purse that stays the same size while the bread inside it shrinks.
abstract.cn: 想象钱袋大小不变，里面的面包却越变越小。

examples.en: Central banks raise rates when inflation refuses to fall.
examples.cn: 当通胀迟迟不降时，央行会加息。

examples.en: Household surveys show that inflation is felt most sharply in food prices.
examples.cn: 家庭调查显示，通胀在食品价格上感受最尖锐。

examples.en: The report blamed wage inflation for the rise in service costs.
examples.cn: 报告把服务成本上升归因于工资推动的物价上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（向内）+ flat（气）+ ion」——往里面打气，越打越鼓 → 膨胀、通胀

root: 拉丁 inflare「吹入、使鼓起」= in-「进入」+ flare「吹」→ 名词 inflatio「吹入、肿胀」→ 英语 inflation；经济义为 19 世纪比喻用法，最早书证存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: air is blown into something, it swells, and the same swelling is then applied to prices, to a measured rate, to demand, to costs and finally to a runaway spiral.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把气吹入某物，它鼓起来；同一个「鼓起」再依次用于物价、一个测得的比率、需求、成本，最后是失控的螺旋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon blown fuller and fuller while the same purse buys less bread.
core.cn: 核心意象：气球越吹越满，同一个钱袋买到的面包却越来越少。

branches.en: PRICE AND RATE: the swollen level of prices is then expressed as a percentage.
branches.cn: 物价与比率：鼓起的物价水平随后被表示为一个百分数。

branches.en: AIR AND BODY: the physical act of blowing fills a thing, and the thing bulges.
branches.cn: 气与物体：吹入的物理动作把东西充满，东西便鼓起。

branches.en: LANGUAGE: the same swelling shows up in speech as exaggeration and self-praise.
branches.cn: 语言：同一种「鼓起」在言语中表现为夸大与自夸。

branches.en: DEMAND AND COST: prices can be pushed from the buyer's side or pulled from the producer's side.
branches.cn: 需求与成本：物价可由买方一侧推起，也可由生产者一侧拉起。

branches.en: RUNAWAY: at the extreme the balloon bursts into hyperinflation.
branches.cn: 失控：到了极端，气球炸成恶性通胀。

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a Latin noun suffix; each piece also builds other English words, and the family has a mirror image in de-.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个拉丁名词后缀构成；每一段还构成别的英语词，整个词族还有一个以 de- 开头的镜像形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin flare 'to blow' gives inflate, inflation, deflate, deflation and flatus; in- and de- set the two directions of the same image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 flare「吹」衍生出 inflate、inflation、deflate、deflation 与 flatus；in- 与 de- 标出同一意象的两个方向。

items.example: The prefix points the blowing inward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「吹」指向内部。

items.example: The root carries the idea of moving air.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「推动空气」的意思。

items.meaning: to blow into; to puff up
items.example: The compound names both the act and its swelling result.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式既指动作，也指其鼓胀的结果。

items.example: The Latin noun supplied the English word directly.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词直接提供了英语词。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.meaning: to fill with air; to raise prices
items.example: Dealers inflate prices before a sale.
items.exampleCN: 商家会在促销前抬高价格。

items.meaning: to let air out; to lower prices
items.example: The mirror verb was formed by swapping the prefix.
items.exampleCN: 这个镜像动词是靠替换前缀造出的。

items.example: The adjective describes pressure, not the rise itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述压力，而非上涨本身。

definition_zh: 影响；影响力；势力；施加影响；（酒、药物的）作用
definition_en: the power to affect people or things, or a hidden force that flows into them and changes them
core_image: 看不见的星力像水一样从天上流下来，注进一个人的身体，悄悄改变他的性情与命运
scene: 老屋里，奶奶的针线笸箩摆在桌上，孙女也拿起了针线。Her grandmother's influence made her fall in love with sewing.
sceneCN: 这里 influence 是「潜移默化的影响」（第 4 个义项：长期而不可见的感化）；句意：祖母的信对她选择当作家的决定有一种安静的影响。画面里有旧信件、书桌和窗外的光。

derivatives.zh: 流行性感冒（旧说由星力致病）

senses.title: Unseen power: the force that changes things
senses.titleCN: 影响力：改变人与事的那股无形之力
senses.definition: the power that someone or something has to affect people, events, or things
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物影响他人、事件或事物的力量
senses.example: Her teacher had a lasting influence on her career.
senses.exampleCN: 她的老师对她的事业产生了持久的影响。
senses.why: The noun is first recorded in late 14c. as an astrological term for a power streaming down from the stars. That invisible force became any unseen power that produces an effect, and by the 1650s it was 'capacity for producing effects by invisible means'.
senses.whyCN: 名词最早记录于 14 世纪后期，是占星术语，指从星辰流下的力量。这种看不见的力后来指任何产生效果的无形之力；到 17 世纪 50 年代，它指“以无形方式产生效果的能力”。

senses.title: To affect: let the current do its work
senses.titleCN: 施加影响：让那股流自己起作用
senses.definition: to affect someone or something, especially in an indirect or gradual way
senses.definitionCN: 影响某人或某物，尤指以间接或渐进的方式
senses.example: Parents influence how their children handle failure.
senses.exampleCN: 父母影响着孩子如何面对失败。
senses.why: The verb appears in the 1650s, converted straight from the noun: to influence is to let that inflowing force act on someone. English often turns a noun for a force into a verb for using it.
senses.whyCN: 动词出现于 17 世纪 50 年代，直接由名词转化而来：influence 就是让那股流入的力作用在某人身上。英语常把一个表示“力”的名词直接变成“使用这股力”的动词。

senses.title: Personal pull: power that opens doors
senses.titleCN: 势力、门路：能替人开门的权力
senses.definition: the power to affect decisions that comes from position, wealth, or personal connections
senses.definitionCN: 来自地位、财富或人脉的、能左右决策的权力
senses.example: He used his influence to get the proposal onto the agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 他动用自己的势力把这项提案送上了议程。
senses.why: By the 1580s the word covered 'exertion of unseen influence by persons', a sense already present in Medieval Latin. When the invisible power is attached to a person's standing, influence becomes the pull that connections give.
senses.whyCN: 到 16 世纪 80 年代，这个词已包含“人施加无形影响”的义项，中世纪拉丁语里已有此义。当那股无形之力附着在某个人的地位上，influence 就成了人脉带来的“拉动力”，即势力。

senses.title: Slow shaping: the force that seeps into character
senses.titleCN: 潜移默化：渗进性情里的那股力
senses.definition: a gradual, often unnoticed effect on someone's character or thinking
senses.definitionCN: 对某人性格或思想缓慢而往往不被察觉的作用
senses.example: Her calm influence changed the tone of the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉稳的性情潜移默化地改变了整个团队的氛围。
senses.why: The oldest image is fluid: influence flows in like water and seeps into character without a single visible act. This is why the word suits slow moral or educational shaping better than sudden persuasion.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是液体：影响像水一样流入，不必有哪一个看得见的动作，就渗进了性情。所以这个词更适合形容缓慢的道德或教育塑造，而不是突然的说服。

senses.title: Star-power: the astrological birth sense
senses.titleCN: 星体流射：占星术里的本义
senses.definition: in old astrology, a power believed to stream from the stars into a person's character or fate
senses.definitionCN: 旧时占星术所信的一种力量，认为它从星辰流入人的性格或命运
senses.example: Medieval doctors blamed the planet's influence for the sudden fever.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的医生把这场突发的高烧归咎于那颗行星的星力。
senses.why: This is the word's birth sense (late 14c.): Medieval Latin influentia named a 'flowing in' from the stars, from influere 'to flow into'. The heavens were thought to pour an ethereal substance into human lives.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的出生义（14 世纪后期）：中世纪拉丁语 influentia 指星辰的“流入”，来自 influere“流入”。当时人相信天体会把一种精微物质倾注进人的生命。

senses.title: Under the influence: the substance inside
senses.titleCN: 酒力发作：进到体内的那种东西
senses.definition: the effect of alcohol or drugs on a person, as in the phrase under the influence
senses.definitionCN: 酒精或药物对人的作用，如短语 under the influence
senses.example: He was arrested for driving under the influence.
senses.exampleCN: 他因酒后驾车被捕。
senses.why: 'Under the influence (of alcohol)' is attested by 1866. The old astrological force is now a substance in the blood: it has flowed in and taken over the driver's judgement.
senses.whyCN: “under the influence（受酒精影响）”记录于 1866 年。昔日占星意义上的力，如今成了血液里的一种物质：它流进身体，接管了司机的判断。

senses.title: A factor: the force made countable
senses.titleCN: 影响因素：被数出来的那股力
senses.definition: a factor or variable that affects an outcome, especially in analysis or research
senses.definitionCN: 影响结果的因子或变量，尤用于分析或研究
senses.example: Income is one of the strongest influences on health outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 收入是影响健康结果最强的因素之一。
senses.why: Once influence means any power producing an effect, researchers can count such powers as factors. The unseen flow becomes a measurable variable in a model.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 influence 泛指任何产生效果的力量，研究者就能把这些力量当作因子来计数。看不见的流，在模型里变成了可以测量的变量。

senses.title: To sway: push a decision one way
senses.titleCN: 左右、促使：把决定推向一边
senses.definition: to persuade or sway someone toward a decision, often by pressure or appeal
senses.definitionCN: 说服或左右某人做出某个决定，常带压力或诉求
senses.example: Lobbyists tried to influence the committee's vote.
senses.exampleCN: 游说者试图左右委员会的投票。
senses.why: The verb's 1650s sense 'modify or affect by intangible means' narrows here to directing a decision. To influence a vote is to make the invisible pull decide which way the lever falls.
senses.whyCN: 动词在 17 世纪 50 年代指“以无形方式改变或作用”，这里收窄为“引导一个决定”。左右一次投票，就是让那股看不见的拉力决定杆子往哪边倒。

senses.title: A flowing in: the literal old sense
senses.titleCN: 流入：字面意义上的古义
senses.definition: a flowing in of water or other fluid, an archaic literal sense
senses.definitionCN: 水或其他液体的流入，古旧的实指义
senses.example: The old physician spoke of an influence of humors into the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老医生谈到体液向血液中的流入。
senses.why: Latin influere was literally 'to flow into'. English kept the physical image for centuries beside the figurative one; it survives now mainly in the Latin-shaped doublet influx.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 influere 字面就是“流入”。英语让这个实指意象与比喻义并存了几个世纪；如今它主要活在拉丁形的同源词 influx 里。

intro.en: Influence begins as astrology: a fluid power pouring from the stars into a person. The metaphor of flowing in then spreads to people, institutions, alcohol, and finally statistics.
intro.cn: influence 起于占星：一股流体般的力量从星辰倾注到人身上。“流入”这个隐喻随后扩展到人、机构、酒，最后扩展到统计学。

items.en: Fluere meant 'to flow, stream, run'. Its deeper PIE form *bhleu- 'to swell, overflow' is a reconstruction with no written record, so that step is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: fluere 意为“流动、涌流”。它更深的印欧语形式 *bhleu-“膨胀、溢出”是重构出来的，没有书面记录，因此那一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Influentia meant 'a flowing in', from influere 'to flow into', built from in- 'into' plus fluere 'to flow'. It was used for the astrological emanation of the stars.
items.cn: influentia 意为“流入”，来自 influere“流入”，由 in-“进入”加 fluere“流”构成。它被用来指星辰的占星流射。

items.en: Old French influence carried both 'a flow of water, a flowing in' and 'an emanation from the stars that acts upon one's character and destiny'.
items.cn: 古法语 influence 兼有“水的流入”和“从星辰流出、作用于人的性格与命运的力量”两义。

items.en: The noun is first recorded as an astrological term: 'streaming ethereal power from the stars, acting upon character or destiny'. Middle English still applied it to any outflowing energy, fluid or immaterial.
items.cn: 名词最早记录为占星术语：“从星辰流出的以太之力，作用于性格或命运”。中古英语仍用它指任何流出的能量，无论是有形的流体还是无形的力。

items.en: The sense 'exertion of unseen influence by persons' is from the 1580s; 'capacity for producing effects by insensible or invisible means' from the 1650s. The verb 'to affect by intangible means' also dates from the 1650s.
items.cn: “人施加无形影响”的义项始于 16 世纪 80 年代；“以不可感知或无形的方式产生效果的能力”始于 17 世纪 50 年代。动词“以无形方式影响”同样记录于 17 世纪 50 年代。

items.en: 'Under the influence (of alcohol)' is attested by 1866. The astral fluid has become a substance in the body, completing the word's long journey from sky to bloodstream.
items.cn: “under the influence（受酒精影响）”记录于 1866 年。星体之流变成了体内的一种物质，完成了这个词从天空到血液的漫长旅程。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: wealth; an abundant flow of money or goods. It shares the -fluence ending but takes ad- 'to' rather than in-.
entries.definitionCN: 富足；财富的丰盛流入。它与 influence 共享 -fluence 词尾，但前缀是 ad-“向”而非 in-。

entries.definition: the flu. Italian borrowed the astrological word for an illness blamed on star influence.
entries.definitionCN: 流行性感冒。意大利语借用了这个占星词，用来指被归因于星力的疾病。

entries.definition: a flowing in of people, money, or things. It keeps the physical image that influence turned into a metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 人、钱或物的涌入。它保留了 influence 转成比喻之前的那个实指意象。

entries.definition: a change produced by a cause. It names the result, while influence names the force behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 效果；结果。它命名结果，而 influence 命名背后的那股力。

entries.definition: a powerful or direct effect. It is stronger and more sudden than the slow influence.
entries.definitionCN: 冲击；强烈影响。它比缓慢的 influence 更强、更突然。

entries.definition: to move someone toward one opinion or decision. It matches influence as a verb of persuasion.
entries.definitionCN: 左右；动摇。它对应 influence 作为“说服”的动词义。

entries.definition: the recognized right to give orders or make decisions. It is formal power, not the informal pull of influence.
entries.definitionCN: 权威；职权。它是正式的权力，而非 influence 那种非正式的拉力。

entries.definition: the power to influence decisions, especially in politics or business.
entries.definitionCN: 势力；影响力，尤指政治或商业上的。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin fluere 'to flow', Medieval Latin influentia, and the English words built from the same stream.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 fluere“流”、中世纪拉丁语 influentia，以及从同一股水流里长出的英语词。

normal.en: influence = in- 'into' + fluere 'to flow': a power flows into you and changes what you do.
normal.cn: influence = in-“进入”+ fluere“流”：一股力流进你体内，改变了你的所作所为。

normal.en: The same fluere gives fluent, fluid, influx and confluence: every one of them is about flowing.
normal.cn: 同一个 fluere 给出 fluent、fluid、influx、confluence：每一个都与“流”有关。

normal.en: Influenza is the same word in Italian: the flu was once blamed on an influence from the stars.
normal.cn: influenza 就是同一个词进了意大利语：流感曾被归因于星辰的影响。

normal.en: An influencer is literally a person who pours a current into a crowd.
normal.cn: influencer 字面上就是往人群里注入一股水流的人。

normal.en: under the influence keeps the old image: the drink has flowed in and is now steering.
normal.cn: under the influence 保留了旧意象：酒已经流进体内，正在握着方向盘。

abstract.en: The core is invisible flow: power with no hand, moving like water.
abstract.cn: 核心是看不见的流动：没有手在推，力量却像水一样移动。

abstract.en: It travels from sky to person to number: star-force, personal pull, statistical factor.
abstract.cn: 它从天空走到人，再走到数字：星力、人脉拉力、统计因子。

abstract.en: Influence and influenza are siblings: both imagine something pouring in and taking hold.
abstract.cn: influence 与 influenza 是同一家的：两者都想象某种东西倾注进来并占据身体。

examples.en: Social media has a huge influence on how teenagers see themselves.
examples.cn: 社交媒体对青少年如何看待自己有着巨大的影响。

examples.en: The climate strongly influences what crops farmers can grow.
examples.cn: 气候强烈影响农民能种哪些作物。

examples.en: She was under the influence of painkillers when she signed the form.
examples.cn: 她签那份表格时正受到止痛药的作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ flu（flow 流）——一股力流进你心里，把你悄悄改变 → influence 影响

root: 源自拉丁语 fluere“流动”，加 in-“进入”构成 influere“流入”，经中世纪拉丁语 influentia 与古法语进入英语；核心是“看不见的力量像水一样流进人身上”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, all one image: something invisible flows into a person and changes what they do. It begins as star-power, becomes personal pull, then a measurable factor, and finally a legal phrase about alcohol.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共用同一个意象：某种看不见的东西流进一个人，改变他的行为。它从星力开始，变成人脉的拉力，再变成可测量的因子，最后成为关于酒精的法律用语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible current flowing into a person and changing them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股看不见的水流进入一个人，并改变了他。

branches.en: THE UNSEEN CURRENT: the power to affect, and its slow shaping of character.
branches.cn: 无形之流：影响的力量，以及它对性情的缓慢塑造。

branches.en: PERSONAL PULL: influence from standing or connections, and the act of swaying a decision.
branches.cn: 人脉拉力：来自地位或关系的势力，以及左右一个决定的行为。

branches.en: THE LITERAL FLOW: star-emanation, and the old physical flowing in.
branches.cn: 字面之流：星体流射，以及古老的实指流入。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE WITHIN: alcohol or drugs taking over judgement.
branches.cn: 体内之物：酒精或药物接管了判断。

branches.en: THE COUNTABLE FORCE: the verb 'to affect', and the factor counted in an analysis.
branches.cn: 可数的力：动词“影响”，以及分析中被计数的因子。

intro.en: Influence is in- plus flu- plus -ence. Its family shows the prefix in-, con-, af- and ef-, the root flu- 'flow', and the suffixes -ent, -id, -ence and -ly.
intro.cn: influence 是 in- 加 flu- 再加 -ence。它的词族展示前缀 in-、con-、af-、ef-，词根 flu-“流”，以及后缀 -ent、-id、-ence、-ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin fluere 'to flow' is the base of fluent, fluid and influx; with prefixes it yields influere, affluere and effluere, and the noun influentia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fluere“流”是 fluent、fluid、influx 的基础；加前缀又给出 influere、affluere、effluere，以及名词 influentia。

items.meaning: a power that flows in and affects
items.example: His advice had a strong influence on my decision.
items.exampleCN: 他的建议对我的决定有很大影响。

items.meaning: having the power to affect people or events
items.meaningCN: 有影响力的（-ial 形容词后缀）
items.example: She became one of the most influential writers of her time.
items.exampleCN: 她成为那个时代最有影响力的作家之一。

items.meaning: flu, an illness once blamed on astral influence
items.meaningCN: 流行性感冒（源自星力致病说）
items.example: The influenza season begins in late autumn.
items.exampleCN: 流感季从深秋开始。

items.meaning: a flowing in of people or things
items.example: The town grew quickly after an influx of workers.
items.exampleCN: 大批工人涌入后，小镇迅速发展。

items.meaningCN: 流利的（-ent 形容词后缀）
items.example: He is fluent in three languages.
items.exampleCN: 他能流利地说三种语言。

items.meaning: a substance that flows; able to flow
items.example: The patient needs more fluids.
items.exampleCN: 这位病人需要多补充液体。

items.meaning: the place where two streams flow together
items.meaningCN: 汇流处（con- 共同 + 流）
items.example: The city stands at the confluence of two rivers.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市位于两条河的交汇处。

items.example: The family lived in comfort but not affluence.
items.exampleCN: 这家人生活舒适，但算不上富足。

items.meaning: liquid waste flowing out of a place
items.meaningCN: 废水；流出物（ef- 向外 + 流）
items.example: The factory was fined for dumping effluent into the river.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂因向河里排放废水而被罚款。

items.example: She speaks Japanese fluently.
items.exampleCN: 她日语说得很流利。

definition_zh: 通知；告诉；告发
definition_en: to give someone facts or knowledge, or to tell an authority about a crime or wrongdoing
core_image: 把消息递到对方手里：让对方从不知道变为知道
scene: 办公室里，助理拿着刚打印的通知快步走向经理的桌子。Please inform the manager that the meeting has been moved to tomorrow morning.
sceneCN: 这里 inform 是「通知」（第 1 个义项：把事实或消息告诉某人）；句意：请通知经理会议已改到明早。

collocations.zh: 消息灵通的；见多识广的

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「信息；情报」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「提供信息的；有益的」
由动词加施动者后缀构成，义为「告密者；线人」
由形容词义加否定前缀构成，义为「非正式的」
由过去分词加副词构成，义为「见识广的」

senses.title: To give someone facts or news
senses.definition: to tell someone about something, giving them facts they did not have
senses.definitionCN: 把对方原本不知道的事实或消息告诉某人
senses.example: Please inform me of any changes to the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 日程如有变动请通知我。
senses.why: The Latin root means to give shape to, and giving facts shapes what a person knows.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本义是「赋予形状」，把事实交给别人，正是在塑造对方的认知。

senses.title: To shape or guide something such as a decision
senses.definition: to have a strong effect on ideas, decisions, or attitudes
senses.definitionCN: 强烈影响思想、决定或态度
senses.example: Her rural childhood informed every novel she wrote.
senses.exampleCN: 她在乡下的童年影响了她写的每一部小说。
senses.why: From shaping knowledge it is a short step to shaping judgment and creative work.
senses.whyCN: 从「塑造认知」到「塑造判断与创作」，只有一步之遥。

senses.title: To tell an authority about wrongdoing
senses.definition: to tell the police or another authority that someone has done something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 向警方或有关部门举报他人的违法行为
senses.example: Someone informed against the smugglers at the port.
senses.exampleCN: 有人告发了港口的走私者。
senses.why: Informing an authority is informing in the official direction: facts flow upward to power.
senses.whyCN: 向官方通报，是把事实向上递交给权力，属同一动作的官方走向。

intro.en: Inform comes from a Latin verb meaning to give form or shape to something.
intro.cn: inform 源自一个拉丁动词，本义是「赋予形式」。

items.en: Latin informare meant to give form to, to shape, built on forma (shape, figure).
items.cn: 拉丁语 informare 意为「赋形、塑造」，建立在 forma（形状）之上。

items.en: In late Latin the verb also came to mean to instruct and train the mind.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中该动词又引申为教导、训练心智。

items.en: Old French adopted it as enfourmer and informer with both shaping and teaching senses.
items.cn: 古法语借入为 enfourmer 与 informer，兼具塑造与教导两义。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century, first about shaping the mind with teaching.
items.cn: 英语于十四世纪引入，最初指以教导塑造心智。

items.en: The senses narrowed to giving facts and news, with the report-a-crime sense appearing by the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 词义收窄为提供事实与消息，举报义至十六世纪前后出现。

note.en: Watch the shape-root family and the close reporting words.

senses.title: Facts about something
senses.titleCN: 信息：关于某人某事的实情
senses.definition: facts or details that tell you about a person, place, event, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 说明某人、某地、某事件或某情况的实情或细节
senses.example: The website gives information about local bus routes.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网站提供本地公交线路的信息。
senses.why: Latin informatio first meant the act of shaping the mind, then the idea placed there. The modern 'facts' sense is a nineteenth-century narrowing: what is communicated is treated as a body of well-shaped facts.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 informatio 最初指给头脑塑形的动作，后来指放进去的观念。现代「事实」义是 19 世纪的收窄：被传递的内容被当成一套已经塑好形状的事实。

senses.title: Knowledge received and kept

senses.definition: knowledge or understanding that someone has received or learned

senses.example: His lectures are full of information about Roman engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 他的讲座充满关于罗马工程的知识。
senses.why: To inform is to give form to a mind. What the mind receives and keeps is information in the older, educational sense of the word.
