senses.title: What a message carries
senses.titleCN: 信息内容：一条消息里真正传过去的东西
senses.definition: the meaningful content of a message or signal, especially in communication theory
senses.definitionCN: 消息或信号中有意义的内容，尤用于通信理论
senses.example: A clear signal carries more information than a noisy one.
senses.exampleCN: 清晰的信号比嘈杂的信号携带更多信息。
senses.why: In information theory, information is whatever reduces uncertainty in a message. The old core survives: a signal must take a definite shape before it can carry meaning.
senses.whyCN: 在信息论中，信息就是减少消息不确定性的东西。旧的核心仍在：信号必须先取得确定的形状，才能承载意义。

senses.title: Data in a computer
senses.titleCN: （计算机）数据；信息：机器能读的形状
senses.definition: data that is stored, processed, or transmitted by a computer
senses.definitionCN: 由计算机存储、处理或传输的数据
senses.example: The server stores information about every login.
senses.exampleCN: 服务器存储每一次登录的信息。
senses.why: A computer keeps data in fixed forms; information is data that has been given a form a machine or reader can use. The suffix -ation marks the result of shaping.
senses.whyCN: 计算机以固定的形式保存数据；信息就是被赋予机器或读者可用的形式的数据。后缀 -ation 标记的正是塑形的结果。

senses.title: Intelligence gathered for a purpose
senses.titleCN: 情报：为某个目的收集来的信息
senses.definition: facts gathered about an enemy, a competitor, or a situation, often secretly
senses.definitionCN: 关于敌人、竞争者或局势而收集的事实，常带秘密性质
senses.example: Military information was passed to headquarters by radio.
senses.exampleCN: 军事情报通过无线电传到了总部。
senses.why: Intelligence is information gathered for a purpose. The flow is the same, but the channel is hidden and the receiver is chosen.
senses.whyCN: 情报是为特定目的收集的信息。流还是同一股流，只是渠道隐蔽了，接收者也经过挑选。

senses.title: Formal notice given to someone
senses.titleCN: 通知；告知：正式递到手上的消息
senses.definition: a formal statement or notice that tells someone something official
senses.definitionCN: 向某人说明官方事务的正式陈述或通知
senses.example: Please contact us for further information about your application.
senses.exampleCN: 欲知申请的进一步通知，请联系我们。
senses.why: A formal notice is information delivered on the record, so that the receiver is officially shaped by it. The act and the content share one noun.
senses.whyCN: 正式通知是有记录地送达的信息，使接收者在官方意义上被它塑形。动作与内容共用同一个名词。

senses.title: Material laid before an inquiry
senses.titleCN: 资料；材料：摆到桌面上供判断的东西
senses.definition: particulars or evidence supplied for an investigation or decision
senses.definitionCN: 为调查或决定而提供的细节或证据材料
senses.example: The panel based its finding on information from eyewitnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 小组根据目击者提供的材料作出判断。
senses.why: In inquiries, information is the shaped material laid before a decision-maker. It is not yet proof; it is what proof will be built from.
senses.whyCN: 在调查中，信息是摆到决策者面前的成形材料。它还不是证据，而是证据将被搭建出来的原料。

senses.title: A service that answers questions
senses.titleCN: 问讯处；资讯服务：把消息指给该去的人
senses.definition: a place or service whose job is to give facts to people who ask
senses.definitionCN: 负责向提问者提供事实的场所或服务
senses.example: Ask at the information desk near the main entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 请到正门附近的问讯处咨询。
senses.why: The desk is named for the act of informing: a place where the flow of facts is directed to whoever asks. The abstract noun stands for the concrete service.
senses.whyCN: 问讯处以 informing 这个动作为名：在这里，事实的水流被引向提问的人。抽象名词转指具体的服务。

senses.title: A formal accusation in law
senses.titleCN: （法律）告发；起诉：把指控写成正式形状
senses.definition: in English law, a formal statement of an offence presented to a court
senses.definitionCN: 在英国法中，向法庭正式提出的犯罪陈述
senses.example: The case began with an information filed against the company.
senses.exampleCN: 案件始于对该公司提出的一份正式告发。
senses.why: In English law an information is a formal statement of an offence laid before a magistrate. The accusation has been given a legal form, which is exactly what informatio meant.
senses.whyCN: 在英国法中，information 是提交治安法官的正式犯罪陈述。指控被赋予了法律形式，这正是 informatio 的本义。

intro.en: Information comes from Latin informatio, a noun of action from informare 'to give shape to, form, instruct'. The word's spine is forma, 'shape': to inform is to put a shape into something, especially a mind. The modern 'facts' sense is a later narrowing.
intro.cn: information 来自拉丁 informatio，是动词 informare「塑形、教导」的行为名词。它的脊梁是 forma「形状」：inform 就是把形状放进某物，尤其是放进头脑。现代「事实」义是后来收窄的结果。

items.en: forma meant 'shape, figure, mould'. A potter's forma is the mould that gives clay its outline; the word already contains the idea of a shape imposed from outside.
items.cn: forma 意为「形状、外形、模子」。陶工的 forma 是给黏土定轮廓的模子；这个词本身已含有「从外部加上的形状」这一观念。

items.en: informare is in- 'into' plus forma: to give a form to something, to mould it. By extension it came to mean 'to form the mind, instruct, teach'.
items.cn: informare 是 in-「向内」加 forma：把形状给予某物、塑造它。引申后意为「塑造头脑、教导、传授」。

items.en: informatio named the act of shaping and, by metonymy, the shape or idea produced: a conception, an outline, an instruction.
items.cn: informatio 指塑形的动作，并以转喻指所产生的形状或观念：概念、轮廓、教导。

items.en: Old French information passed into English in the fourteenth century. Early English information meant instruction, news, or the act of informing, not a mass of neutral facts.
items.cn: 古法语 information 在 14 世纪进入英语。早期英语的 information 指教导、消息或告知的行为，而不是一堆中性的事实。

items.en: The modern sense 'facts communicated' is generally regarded as a nineteenth-century development, pushed by newspapers, telegraphy, and organized science, which needed a word for transferable factual content.
items.cn: 现代「被传递的事实」义一般被认为是 19 世纪的发展，由报纸、电报与有组织的科学推动——它们需要一个词来指可转移的事实内容。

items.en: In the twentieth century information became a measurable quantity in communication theory (1948) and then the ordinary word for data handled by machines.
items.cn: 20 世纪，information 在通信理论（1948 年）中成为可度量的量，随后又成为机器所处理数据的日常用词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin base forma or the verb informare; the last item, informal, looks identical in prefix but belongs to a different in-. The second group holds words that overlap in content but differ in origin and scope.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词基 forma 或动词 informare；最后一项 informal 前缀形似，却属于另一个 in-。第二组是内容上重叠、但来源与范围不同的词。

entries.definition: to tell someone facts; literally to give a form to the mind. It is the verb behind information.
entries.definitionCN: 告知某人事实；字面是给头脑塑形。它是 information 所依据的动词。

entries.definition: giving useful facts. It describes the source or content, while information names the content itself.
entries.definitionCN: 提供有用事实的。它描述来源或内容，而 information 指内容本身。

entries.definition: a person who supplies information, often secretly to an investigator. The -ant suffix marks the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 提供信息的人，常指向调查者秘密提供信息者。-ant 后缀标记施动者。

entries.definition: relaxed, not official. It is in- 'not' plus formalis 'formal', not in- 'into' plus forma. The two prefixes are unrelated in sense here.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式的；放松的。它是 in-「不」加 formalis「正式的」，不是 in-「向内」加 forma。此处两个前缀意义无关。

entries.definition: facts and figures collected for reference or analysis. Data is raw material; information is data given meaning or form.
entries.definitionCN: 为参考或分析而收集的事实与数字。data 是原料，information 是被赋予意义或形式的数据。

entries.definition: organized understanding that a person or group possesses. Information can sit in a file; knowledge lives in a mind.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体拥有的成体系理解。信息可以躺在文件里，知识则活在头脑中。

entries.definition: information collected about an enemy or a situation, especially by secret means. Narrower and more purposeful than information.
entries.definitionCN: 关于敌人或局势而收集的信息，尤指通过秘密手段。比 information 更窄、更有目的性。

entries.definition: newly received information about recent events. News is time-bound; information need not be new.
entries.definitionCN: 关于近期事件的新消息。news 受时间约束，information 则不必是新的。

normalIntro.en: The family is one act of shaping: forma is the mould, inform is to press the shape in, information is the shape that remains.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词族就是一次塑形：forma 是模子，inform 是把形状压进去，information 是留下的形状。

normal.en: in- 'into' + forma 'shape': to inform a mind is to press a shape into it, and information is that shape once it is there.
normal.cn: in-「向内」+ forma「形状」：inform 一个头脑，就是把形状压进去；information 就是留在里面的那个形状。

normal.en: -ation (Latin -atio) is the noun suffix of an action and its result: inform → information.
normal.cn: -ation（拉丁 -atio）是表示动作及其结果的名词后缀：inform → information。

normal.en: The early meaning was instruction, not neutral facts; the 'facts' sense is a modern narrowing.
normal.cn: 早期词义是教导，不是中性事实；「事实」义是后来的收窄。

normal.en: informal is a false friend: in- there means 'not', and the base is formal, not form.
normal.cn: informal 是假朋友：那里的 in- 意为「不」，词基是 formal，不是 form。

normal.en: A computer's information is data that has been given a form a machine can hold.
normal.cn: 计算机的信息，就是被赋予机器可保存之形式的数据。

abstract.en: Think of clay on a wheel: the raw facts are clay, and information is the pot that has taken a shape.
abstract.cn: 想象陶轮上的黏土：原始事实是泥，信息是已经成形的陶罐。

abstract.en: Think of a library where every fact has a label and a shelf: the label is what turns a pile of papers into information.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每条事实都有标签和书架位置：标签就是把一叠纸变成信息的东西。

abstract.en: Think of a signal crossing a noisy room: information is the part that still arrives and reduces your uncertainty.
abstract.cn: 想象一个信号穿过嘈杂的房间：信息就是仍然抵达、并减少你不确定性的那部分。

examples.en: The guidebook contains practical information about trains, ferries, and local markets.
examples.cn: 这本指南包含关于火车、渡船和本地市场的实用信息。

examples.en: The company encrypts all personal information before it leaves the server.
examples.cn: 公司在个人信息离开服务器前将其全部加密。

examples.en: Under English law, an information may be laid before a magistrate to begin proceedings.
examples.cn: 根据英国法，可以向治安法官提交正式告发以启动程序。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: in（向内）+ form（形状）+ ation（名词）——把形状放进头脑，头脑里留下的那个形状就是「信息」；纸上的事实被整理成形，也就成了可查找的「资料」。

root: 拉丁 informare「塑形、教导」（in-「向内」+ forma「形状」）→ 拉丁 informatio「概念、教导」→ 古法语 information → 英语 information；-ation 为拉丁 -atio 名词后缀。现代「事实」义一般认为是 19 世纪随报刊、电报与科学兴起而固定。注意 informal 的 in- 是「不」，与此处 in-「向内」不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all come from one act: giving a shape. A mind is shaped by teaching, a message by a definite form, a computer file by a format, a court by a formal accusation.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都出自同一个动作：赋予形状。头脑被教导塑形，消息被确定的形式塑形，计算机文件被格式塑形，法庭被正式指控塑形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: raw material pressed into a form that someone can read and use.
core.cn: 核心意象：原料被压成某种形状，好让别人读懂、使用。

branches.en: FACTS AND KNOWLEDGE: shaped facts about the world, and what a mind keeps after being shaped.
branches.cn: 事实与知识：关于世界的成形事实，以及头脑被塑形后留下的东西。

branches.en: FORM IN TRANSIT: the meaningful content of a signal, and data given a machine-readable form.
branches.cn: 传递中的形式：信号里有意义的内容，以及被赋予机器可读形式的数据。

branches.en: PURPOSEFUL FLOW: facts gathered for a purpose, and notice officially delivered.
branches.cn: 有目的的流动：为特定目的收集的事实，以及正式送达的通知。

branches.en: BEFORE A DECISION: material laid before an inquiry, and a desk that directs facts to askers.
branches.cn: 决定之前：摆到调查者面前的料，以及把事实引向提问者的问讯处。

branches.en: THE LEGAL FORM: an accusation given the shape the court requires.
branches.cn: 法律的形式：被赋予法庭所需形状的一项指控。

intro.en: Information is a Latinate noun: informare plus -atio. The suffix builds action-and-result nouns; the prefix in- and the base forma remain visible inside. The same base produces inform, informative, informed, and informant.
intro.cn: information 是拉丁系名词：informare 加 -atio。这个后缀构成「动作及其结果」名词；前缀 in- 与词基 forma 在词内仍可辨认。同一词基还产生 inform、informative、informed 与 informant。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma 'shape, mould' is the source of information, inform, informative, and also of formal and format. Note that English informal uses a homonymous in- meaning 'not', not the in- 'into' of informare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 forma「形状、模子」是 information、inform、informative 以及 formal、format 的来源。注意英语 informal 用的是同形的 in-「不」，而不是 informare 的 in-「向内」。

items.meaning: to give shape to, especially the mind; to tell
items.meaningCN: 塑形，尤指塑造头脑；告知
items.example: Please inform us of any change of address.
items.exampleCN: 地址如有变更，请通知我们。

items.meaning: the act of shaping or instructing; what is communicated
items.meaningCN: 塑形或教导的行为；被传递的内容
items.example: The file contains information on every supplier.
items.exampleCN: 这份档案包含关于每家供应商的信息。

items.meaningCN: 提供有用事实或知识的
items.example: The museum tour was short but informative.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆的导览虽短，却很有信息量。

items.meaningCN: 已获知事实的；有见识的
items.example: An informed reader will notice the missing figure.
items.exampleCN: 有见识的读者会注意到缺失的数字。

items.meaning: in a way that gives useful facts
items.meaningCN: 以提供有用事实的方式
items.example: The chart is informatively labelled.
items.exampleCN: 这张图表的标注提供了有用的信息。

items.meaning: the quality of giving useful information
items.example: Readers rated the article's informativeness highly.
items.exampleCN: 读者对这篇文章的信息量评价很高。

items.example: The police protected the identity of their informant.
items.exampleCN: 警方保护了线人的身份。

items.example: The debate was dominated by uninformed guesses.
items.exampleCN: 这场辩论被不知情的猜测主导。

items.meaning: relaxed, unofficial; a different in- from inform
items.meaningCN: 非正式的；放松的（in- 意为「不」，与 inform 的 in- 不同）
items.example: They reached an informal agreement over lunch.
items.exampleCN: 他们在午餐时达成了一项非正式协议。

latinEntries.meaning: to shape, mould, form the mind

definition_zh: 最初的；开始的；首字母；姓名缩写；用首字母签署
definition_en: belonging to the beginning, or the first letter of a word or name
core_image: 一本书的第一页第一行，第一个字母被放大成金色花纹，后面的一切都从它开始
scene: 档案室里，编辑用笔圈出每份签名开头的那个字母。The editor circled the initial letter of each name in the document.
sceneCN: 这里 initials 是「姓名首字母缩写」（第 3 个义项：用名字开头的字母代表全名）；句意：在这张表上写下你的姓名缩写就行。画面里有表格、笔和圈出的字母。

pos.zh: 首字母；姓名缩写；装饰性首字母

senses.title: At the start: the first moment
senses.titleCN: 最初的：时间上的第一步
senses.definition: happening at the beginning; first in a series
senses.definitionCN: 发生在开始时的；一系列中的第一个
senses.example: The initial results look promising.
senses.exampleCN: 初步结果看起来很有希望。
senses.why: The adjective is recorded from the 1520s as 'of or pertaining to a beginning'. Latin initialis came from initium 'a beginning', literally 'a going in' — the first step into something.
senses.whyCN: 形容词记录于 16 世纪 20 年代，意为“与开始有关的”。拉丁语 initialis 来自 initium“开始”，字面是“一次走入”——踏进某事的第一步。

senses.title: The first letter: where a word steps in
senses.titleCN: 首字母：一个词进门的地方
senses.definition: the first letter of a word or name
senses.definitionCN: 单词或姓名的第一个字母
senses.example: The poem's initials are decorated in gold.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗的首字母用金色装饰。
senses.why: The noun is recorded from the 1620s, shortened from the adjective in the specialized phrase 'initial letter'. A letter standing at the start of a word takes the name of the start itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词记录于 17 世纪 20 年代，是由短语 initial letter“开头的字母”中形容词的专指用法而来。站在一个词开头的字母，就直接借用了“开头”这个名字。

senses.title: Initials: several beginnings as one name
senses.titleCN: 姓名缩写：几个开头合成一个名字
senses.definition: the first letters of a person's names, used together to stand for the full name
senses.definitionCN: 一个人各名字的首字母合在一起，代表全名
senses.example: Please write your initials beside each correction.
senses.exampleCN: 请在每处修改旁写上你的姓名缩写。
senses.why: Once a single initial marks a word, the set of such letters can mark a whole name. The plural initials turns several beginnings into a compact signature.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个 initial 能标记一个词的开头，那么一组这样的字母就能标记整个姓名。复数 initials 把好几个“开头”压成一个紧凑的签名。

senses.title: To initial: sign with the first letters
senses.titleCN: 签首字母：用开头的字母代替签名
senses.definition: to mark or sign something with one's initials
senses.definitionCN: 用自己的姓名首字母标记或签署某物
senses.example: He initialed every page of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他在合同的每一页上签了姓名首字母。
senses.why: The verb is recorded from 1837, formed directly from the noun: to put the first letters where a full signature would go, a quick legal mark.
senses.whyCN: 动词记录于 1837 年，直接由名词构成：在本该写全名的地方写下开头的字母，是一种快捷的法律标记。

senses.title: At the front: a matter of position
senses.titleCN: 词首的、句首的：说的是位置而非时间
senses.definition: standing at the beginning of a word, sentence, or line
senses.definitionCN: 位于单词、句子或诗行的开头
senses.example: An initial consonant often carries the stress in English words.
senses.exampleCN: 英语单词的词首辅音常常承载重音。
senses.why: The 1620s adjective also meant 'standing at the beginning of a word, sentence, etc.' Here initial names a position, not a time: whatever occupies the front slot is initial.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 20 年代的形容词也指“位于词、句的开头”。这里 initial 命名的是位置而不是时间：占据最前面那个位置的，就是 initial。

senses.title: Initial sound: the consonant at the gate
senses.titleCN: 声母：守在音节门口的那个音
senses.definition: in phonetics, the sound or consonant at the start of a syllable
senses.definitionCN: 语音学上，音节开头的音或辅音
senses.example: Mandarin syllables are analysed as an initial and a final.
senses.exampleCN: 普通话的音节被分析为声母和韵母两部分。
senses.why: Phonology borrowed the positional sense: the initial is the consonant that opens a syllable, the part that stands at the gate before the vowel.
senses.whyCN: 音系学借走了那个位置义：声母是打开一个音节的那个辅音，是在韵母之前守在门口的部分。

senses.title: Early stage: the first, faint signs
senses.titleCN: 初期的：最早、最轻的那些迹象
senses.definition: early in a process, before later stages develop
senses.definitionCN: 处于过程的早期，后阶段尚未展开
senses.example: Initial symptoms of the disease are easy to miss.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病的初期症状很容易被忽略。
senses.why: From 'belonging to a beginning', medicine takes initial for the first, often faint stage of an illness. The later stages exist, but this is what shows at the door.
senses.whyCN: 医学从“属于开头”这一层取用 initial，指疾病最初、往往很轻的阶段。后面的阶段当然存在，但这一刻在门口露面的只是它。

senses.title: Starting setting: the value before change
senses.titleCN: 初始设置：改变之前的值
senses.definition: in computing and mathematics, the value or setting that exists at the start of a process
senses.definitionCN: 计算机或数学中，过程开始时就存在的值或设置
senses.example: You can restore the program to its initial settings.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以把程序恢复到初始设置。
senses.why: Modern technical use extends 'at the beginning' to a state before any change: initial conditions, initial settings. The word names the baseline from which a process runs.
senses.whyCN: 现代技术用法把“在开头”延伸到“任何改变之前的状态”：初始条件、初始设置。这个词命名的是一个过程启动时所依据的基线。

senses.title: The illuminated initial: a letter turned into a picture
senses.titleCN: 装饰首字母：被画成一幅画的那个字母
senses.definition: a large decorated letter at the start of a chapter in an old manuscript or printed book
senses.definitionCN: 古代手抄本或印本中，章节开头的大型装饰字母
senses.example: The illuminated initial shows a knight on horseback.
senses.exampleCN: 那个装饰首字母画着一位骑马的骑士。
senses.why: Medieval scribes enlarged the first letter of a chapter into a picture. The decorated initial is sense 02 given space and gold, marking where the text begins.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪抄写员把一章的第一个字母放大成一幅画。装饰首字母就是把第 2 义给了空间和金色，标记正文从哪里开始。

intro.en: Initial is built on the Latin verb inire 'to go into'. A beginning is literally a going in: one crosses a threshold, and the first letter of a word or name stands at that threshold.
intro.cn: initial 建在拉丁动词 inire“走进去”上。“开始”字面上就是“走进”：人跨过一道门槛，而单词或姓名的第一个字母就站在那道门槛上。

items.en: Inire meant 'to go into, enter upon, begin', from in- 'into' plus ire 'to go'. The deeper PIE root *ei- 'to go' is a reconstruction, so that step is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: inire 意为“走入、着手、开始”，由 in-“进入”加 ire“走”构成。更深的印欧语词根 *ei-“走”是重构形式，因此那一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Initium meant 'a beginning, a commencement; an entrance, a going in'. It is a noun use of the neuter past participle of inire, so the word carries the image of having stepped inside.
items.cn: initium 意为“开始、开端；入口、一次走入”。它是 inire 中性过去分词的名词化用法，所以这个词自带“已经跨进去”的画面。

items.en: Initialis meant 'initial, incipient, of the beginning', derived from initium. Latin gave the adjective to French and to English.
items.cn: initialis 意为“开头的、初期的、属于开始的”，由 initium 派生。拉丁语把这个形容词传给了法语和英语。

items.en: The adjective is recorded as 'of or pertaining to a beginning', borrowed from French initial or directly from Latin initialis.
items.cn: 形容词记录为“与开始有关的”，借自法语 initial，或直接来自拉丁语 initialis。

items.en: The noun appears as 'initial letter of a name or surname', from a specialized use of the adjective meaning 'standing at the beginning of a word, sentence, etc.'
items.cn: 名词出现，意为“姓名或姓氏的首字母”，来自形容词“位于词、句开头”的专指用法。

items.en: The verb 'to mark or sign with initials' is recorded from 1837, formed from the noun. Related forms are initialed and initialing in American spelling.
items.cn: 动词“用首字母标记或签署”记录于 1837 年，由名词构成。美式拼写中相关形式为 initialed、initialing。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the ability to act first without being told. It is initi- plus -ative, from the same initium.
entries.definitionCN: 主动性；率先行动的能力。它是 initi- 加 -ative，同出 initium。

entries.definition: at first; at the beginning. It is initial plus -ly and differs only in the ending.
entries.definitionCN: 起初；最初。它是 initial 加 -ly，只差词尾。

entries.definition: to begin something or bring someone into a group. It swaps the -ial ending for -iate.
entries.definitionCN: 开始；使入门。它把 -ial 词尾换成 -iate。

entries.definition: coming before all others in time or order. It is the plain English word for initial.
entries.definitionCN: 第一的；最先的。它是 initial 的朴素英语说法。

entries.definition: the first part or beginning of something. It stresses the moment a thing opens.
entries.definitionCN: 开头；开端。它强调事物“打开”的那一刻。

entries.definition: existing from the beginning, or first in a line. It points to origin rather than mere order.
entries.definitionCN: 最初的；原先的。它指向来源，而不只是顺序上的第一。

entries.definition: just beginning to appear or develop. It is more formal and often used of things not yet visible.
entries.definitionCN: 初期的；刚出现的。它更正式，常指尚未明显显现的事物。

entries.definition: done before the main event as preparation. It is initial in time, but serves something later.
entries.definitionCN: 初步的；预备的。它在时间上最前，但为后来的正事服务。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin inire 'to go in', initium 'a beginning', and the English family of initial, initiate, initiative.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 inire“走进”、initium“开始”，以及 initial、initiate、initiative 这一族英语词。

normal.en: initial = in- 'into' + ire 'to go': the first step is the one that goes in.
normal.cn: initial = in-“进入”+ ire“走”：第一步就是走进门的那一步。

normal.en: initium means 'a going in', so a beginning and an entrance are the same picture.
normal.cn: initium 意为“一次走入”，所以“开始”和“入口”是同一幅画。

normal.en: The initial letter stands at the doorway of a word, which is why the first letter is called an initial.
normal.cn: 首字母站在一个词的门槛上，所以第一个字母才叫 initial。

normal.en: Your initials are several doorways of your name compressed into one mark.
normal.cn: 你的姓名缩写，就是把你名字的几道门槛压成一个记号。

normal.en: initial settings are the values a program has before it has walked anywhere.
normal.cn: initial settings 是一个程序还没走到任何地方时的值。

abstract.en: The core is a threshold: whatever stands just inside the opening is initial.
abstract.cn: 核心是一道门槛：刚跨进门口的那一点，就是 initial。

abstract.en: The same word names a time, a letter, and a position, because all three are 'the front of something'.
abstract.cn: 同一个词命名时间、字母和位置，因为三者都是“某物的最前面”。

abstract.en: Beginning and entering are one idea here: to begin is to step through a door.
abstract.cn: 在这里，“开始”与“进入”是同一个念头：开始就是跨过一道门。

examples.en: The initial estimate was far too low.
examples.cn: 最初的估算远远偏低。

examples.en: Her initials are written in gold on the cover.
examples.cn: 她的姓名首字母用金色写在封面上。

examples.en: The initial stage of the project lasted six months.
examples.cn: 项目的初始阶段持续了六个月。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进入）+ it（go 走）——刚走进门口的那一步 → initial 最初的；首字母

root: 源自拉丁语 initium“开始、进入”，由 inire“走进、开始”而来（in-“进入”+ ire“走”）；核心是“刚跨进门的那一步”，故引申为“最初的”与“首字母”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses built on one threshold: the first moment, the first letter, the letters that sign a name, the front position, the early stage, and the baseline before any change.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都建在一道门槛上：最初的时刻、第一个字母、签名字母、最前面的位置、早期阶段，以及任何改变之前的基线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a threshold; whatever stands at the opening is initial.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门槛；站在门口的一切都是 initial。

branches.en: THE FIRST MOMENT: what happens at the beginning, and the early stage of an illness.
branches.cn: 最初的时刻：开头发生的事，以及疾病的早期阶段。

branches.en: THE FIRST LETTER: the opening letter of a word, and its decorated manuscript form.
branches.cn: 第一个字母：词的开头字母，以及它在手抄本里的装饰形态。

branches.en: THE COMPACT SIGNATURE: initials standing for a name, and the act of signing with them.
branches.cn: 紧凑的签名：代表姓名的首字母，以及用它们签署的动作。

branches.en: THE FRONT SLOT: a letter at the start of a word or sentence, and the initial sound of a syllable.
branches.cn: 最前面的位置：词或句首的字母，以及音节的词首音。

branches.en: THE STARTING STATE: the default value or condition before a process changes it.
branches.cn: 起始状态：过程改变它之前的默认值或条件。

intro.en: Initial is in- plus it- plus -ial. Its family shows the prefix in-, the root it- from ire 'to go', and the suffixes -ial, -ly, -iate, -ion, -ive, -or, -ism and -ize.
intro.cn: initial 是 in- 加 it- 再加 -ial。它的词族展示前缀 in-，来自 ire“走”的词根 it-，以及后缀 -ial、-ly、-iate、-ion、-ive、-or、-ism、-ize。

latinIntro.en: Latin inire 'to go into' gives initium 'a beginning' and initialis 'of the beginning'. The same root produces initiate, initiation and initiative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inire“走入”给出 initium“开始”和 initialis“属于开始的”。同一个词根产生 initiate、initiation、initiative。

items.meaning: of the beginning; the first letter
items.meaningCN: 最初的；首字母（走进门的那一步）
items.example: Our initial plan was too ambitious.
items.exampleCN: 我们最初的计划过于宏大。

items.meaningCN: 起初；最初（-ly 副词后缀）
items.example: Initially, no one believed the story.
items.exampleCN: 起初没有人相信这个故事。

items.meaning: to begin; to bring someone into a practice
items.meaningCN: 开始；使入门（-iate 动词后缀）
items.example: They initiated a new health program.
items.exampleCN: 他们发起了一项新的健康计划。

items.meaning: the act of beginning or admitting a member
items.meaningCN: 开始；入会仪式（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: The club's initiation includes a short test.
items.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部的入会仪式包括一项小测试。

items.meaning: the power to act first; a new plan
items.example: She took the initiative and called the client.
items.exampleCN: 她主动打电话给了客户。

items.example: He was the initiator of the reform.
items.exampleCN: 他是这场改革的发起人。

items.meaning: a word formed from first letters, each sounded separately
items.example: FBI is an initialism, not an acronym.
items.exampleCN: FBI 是首字母缩略词，不是首字母拼音词。

items.meaning: to set a device or program to its starting state
items.example: The system initializes the drive on startup.
items.exampleCN: 系统在启动时会初始化该驱动器。

items.meaning: serving as an introduction or first rite
items.meaningCN: 入门的；起始的（-atory 形容词后缀）
items.example: The initiatory rite lasted three days.
items.exampleCN: 入门仪式持续了三天。

items.meaning: not yet introduced to a group or body of knowledge
items.meaningCN: 未入门的；外行的（un- 否定 + -ed）
items.example: The lecture assumed no knowledge, so the uninitiated could follow.
items.exampleCN: 这场讲座假定听众零基础，所以外行也能听懂。

latinEntries.meaning: to go into, enter upon, begin

definition_zh: 最初；起初；一开始
definition_en: at the beginning of a process or period, before later changes
core_image: 一条跑道的起点白线，前方是尚未跑过的路
scene: 项目启动会上，负责人先回顾最早的安排。Initially, the factory produced only hand tools.
sceneCN: 这里指过程刚开始时的情况（第 2 个义项：句首交代最初阶段）；句意为这家工厂起初只生产手工工具。

senses.title: At the first stage
senses.definition: at the beginning of a process, before later changes
senses.definitionCN: 在过程开始时，后来尚未发生改动之前
senses.example: The building was initially designed as a warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑最初是按仓库设计的。
senses.why: Modifying the verb, it fixes the starting state and leaves room for a later revision.
senses.whyCN: 修饰动词时，它固定了起始状态，并为后来的改动留下余地。

senses.title: Sentence-opening frame
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to set the opening scene of an account
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，为一段叙述搭起开场的场景
senses.example: Initially, no one believed the rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 起初，没有人相信那个传闻。
senses.why: The sentence adverb organizes the order of events for the reader rather than describing how an action was done.
senses.whyCN: 这个句子副词为读者安排事件顺序，而不是描述动作怎么做。

senses.title: First but not now
senses.definition: used to contrast an early state with a later reversal
senses.definitionCN: 用来把早期状态与后来的反转形成对照
senses.example: She initially opposed the merger, then voted for it.
senses.exampleCN: 她起初反对合并，后来却投了赞成票。
senses.why: The word carries an implicature of change: naming the first position invites the reader to expect a second.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带有「后来变了」的言外之意：说出最初的立场，读者自然会期待后文。

senses.title: At the outset of a period
senses.definition: at the very start of a defined period such as a career or project
senses.definitionCN: 在某段明确时期的最开端，如职业生涯或项目
senses.example: The firm initially employed only five people.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司最初只雇了五个人。
senses.why: Here the word anchors a timeline, often with numbers or dates, and does not by itself suggest a reversal.
senses.whyCN: 这里它锚定一条时间线，常与数字或日期连用，本身并不暗示后来的反转。

senses.title: First step in a procedure
senses.definition: used in instructions to mark the first operation in a sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在说明中标记一系列操作的第一步
senses.example: Initially, the sample is heated to a fixed temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 首先，把样品加热到固定温度。
senses.why: Technical writing uses it as a sequence marker, close to first, with the other steps assumed to follow.
senses.whyCN: 技术写作把它当作顺序标记，接近「首先」，并默认后续步骤会接着进行。

senses.title: Originally intended
senses.definition: used with verbs of planning to describe an intention later abandoned
senses.definitionCN: 与计划类动词连用，描述后来被放弃的意图
senses.example: The site was initially intended for a small clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地原本打算建一间小诊所。
senses.why: With plan, intend or design, the word signals unrealized intention rather than a completed early stage.
senses.whyCN: 与「计划、打算、设计」连用时，它暗示意图没有实现，而不是描述已完成的早期阶段。

senses.title: On first impression
senses.definition: used of an impression formed before closer inspection
senses.definitionCN: 用于尚未细看时形成的印象
senses.example: The poem initially looks like a simple folk song.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗初看像一首简单的民歌。
senses.why: The adverb can mark a first reading or impression that later analysis may overturn.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以标记初次阅读或第一印象，而后续分析可能把它推翻。

senses.title: Initial conditions in science
senses.definition: in technical contexts, describing the state of a system at the starting point of an analysis
senses.definitionCN: 在技术语境中，描述系统在分析起点时的状态
senses.example: The model is initially at rest and then subjected to a steady force.
senses.exampleCN: 模型初始时静止，随后受到一个恒定的力。
senses.why: Physics and mathematics use the word for the state assigned at the start of an analysis, a precise technical sense rather than a narrative one.
senses.whyCN: 物理与数学用它指分析起点所设定的状态，这是精确的技术义，而非叙述义。

intro.en: Initially is the Latin adjective for a beginning plus the English adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词是拉丁语「属于开端的」形容词加英语副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The noun initium means a beginning or entrance, and supplies the stem for the whole family.
items.cn: 名词意为「开端、进入」，为整个词族提供词干。

items.en: The verb inire joins in-, meaning into, with ire, to go; literally to go into something.
items.cn: 动词由表示「进入」的前缀与「走」合成，字面是「走进某事物」。

items.en: The adjective initialis, belonging to a beginning, is formed on the noun stem.
items.cn: 形容词由名词词干构成，意为「属于开端的」。

items.en: French initial and English initial carry the adjective into general and technical use.
items.cn: 法语与英语的形容词把它带入通用与技术语境。

items.en: English adds its adverb suffix and uses the form to frame the first stage of an account; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语加副词后缀，用它框定叙述的最初阶段；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern scientific writing fixes initially for the state assigned at the start of an experiment or model.
items.cn: 现代科学写作把它固定为实验或模型开始时所设定的状态。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin beginning-stem; the second group names ways of pointing to the first point in time.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「开端」词干；第二组是指向时间上最初时点的近义说法。

entries.definition: Happening at the beginning; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 发生在开端的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The act of starting something or the ceremony of admission.
entries.definitionCN: 开始某事的行为，或加入仪式的入门礼。

entries.definition: The ability to act first, or a new plan set in motion.
entries.definitionCN: 率先行动的能力，或启动的新计划。

entries.definition: To prepare a system or variable for its first use.
entries.definitionCN: 为系统或变量首次使用作准备；初始化。

entries.definition: At the beginning, especially before a change becomes clear.
entries.definitionCN: 开始时，尤指在变化显现之前。

entries.definition: In the first place, before later alteration.
entries.definitionCN: 原本，在后来改动之前。

entries.definition: At the very beginning of an undertaking.
entries.definitionCN: 在一项工作最开始的时候。

entries.definition: Before anything else in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 在时间或次序上先于其他。

entries.definition: During the first part of a period or process.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时期或过程的前段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real going-in root and the real patterns of planning and science.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「走进」词根，以及计划与科学语境中的真实搭配。

normal.en: The root means to go in, so initially names the moment just inside the door.
normal.cn: 词根意为「走进」，所以「最初」就是刚迈进门口的那一刻。

normal.en: Put it first in a sentence and the story is quietly rewound.
normal.cn: 把它放在句首，故事就被悄悄倒带。

normal.en: Say how things were initially and the reader waits for a later turn.
normal.cn: 先说最初怎样，读者自然会等「后来怎样」。

normal.en: In a laboratory report it is the moment the clock starts.
normal.cn: 在实验报告里，它就是计时器归零的那一瞬。

normal.en: With intend or plan it hints that the intention was later dropped.
normal.cn: 与「打算、计划」连用时，它暗示这个意图后来没照做。

abstract.en: The first stage is not yet the story; it is the position from which the story will be measured.
abstract.cn: 最初阶段还不是故事本身，而是后来用来丈量故事的那个起点。

abstract.en: Naming how something began is already admitting that it did not stay that way.
abstract.cn: 说出某事的开始，本身就已经承认它没有一直如此。

abstract.en: An initial state is a clean sheet that later events will mark.
abstract.cn: 初始状态是一张白纸，等着后来的事件在上面落笔。

examples.en: The committee initially approved the plan, then reversed itself in June.
examples.cn: 委员会起初批准了这项计划，六月又推翻了它。

examples.en: The device is initially calibrated at room temperature.
examples.cn: 这台设备最初在室温下校准。

examples.en: Initially, the course was offered only to graduate students.
examples.cn: 起初，这门课只向研究生开放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一你手里」——一开始手里什么都没有，只是起点

root: 拉丁语名词「开端」来自动词「走进」，在其词干上构成形容词「属于开端的」；英语经法语借入该形容词，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses cover the first stage, the sentence-opening frame, the implication of later change, the start of a period, the first step of a procedure, an abandoned intention, first impression and initial conditions in science.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项覆盖最初阶段、句首框架、后来改变的含义、某段时期的开端、程序第一步、被放弃的意图、初看印象，以及科学中的初始条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white starting line on a track, with the road still unrun ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑道起点的一条白线，前方是尚未跑过的路。

branches.en: THE FIRST STAGE: the starting state of a process before revision.
branches.cn: 最初阶段：过程开始、尚未改动时的状态。

branches.en: THE NARRATIVE FRAME: the sentence-opening marker and the hint of a later reversal.
branches.cn: 叙述框架：句首标记与「后来反转」的暗示。

branches.en: THE PERIOD OUTSET: the first point on a timeline.
branches.cn: 时期开端：时间线上的第一个点。

branches.en: THE PLANNED BEGINNING: the first procedural step and the intention later dropped.
branches.cn: 计划中的开始：程序第一步，以及后来放弃的意图。

branches.en: THE FIRST READING: first impression and the assigned initial state of a system.
branches.cn: 初次判读：初看印象，以及系统被设定的初始状态。

intro.en: Initially is built from the Latin beginning-stem, its adjective suffix and an English adverb suffix; the parts recur across the family.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「开端」词干、形容词后缀与英语副词后缀构成，各构件在同一词族中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: The family starts from the verb for going in and builds a noun of beginning, then an adjective of belonging to the beginning.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从表示「走进」的动词出发，先构成「开端」名词，再构成「属于开端」的形容词。

items.example: The prefix gives the direction of entering.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给出「进入」的方向。

items.example: The verb supplies the movement at the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供整个词族的核心动作。

items.example: The noun turns the movement into a starting point.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把动作转成一个起点。

items.example: The adjective attaches the idea to whatever comes first.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把这一概念系到最先出现的事物上。

items.example: The verb gives the family its noun of initiation.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为词族提供「入门、开始」的名词。

items.example: English keeps the adjective for what comes first.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留这个形容词指最先出现的事物。

items.example: The verb is used for starting a process or admitting a member.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用于发起过程或接纳成员。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a time adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成时间副词。

items.meaning: the act of setting a starting state
items.example: Computing uses the noun for setting a system to its start.
items.exampleCN: 计算机领域用这个名词指把系统设回起始状态。

definition_zh: 主动性；主动权；倡议；首创精神
definition_en: the ability to act first without being told, or a new plan intended to solve a problem
core_image: 不等指令先迈出的第一步：自己把球踢起来
scene: 会议室里，主管刚说完问题还没安排人手，一位组员已起身领了任务。She showed great initiative by starting the project before anyone asked her.
sceneCN: 这里 initiative 是「主动性」（第 1 个义项：没人吩咐就先行动的能力）；句意：没人要求她就开始做项目，展现出很强的主动性。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「开始；发起；使入门」
同根词，义为「最初的；开始的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「开始；入会仪式」
由动词加施动者后缀构成，义为「发起人」

senses.title: Acting first without being told
senses.definition: the ability to decide and act on your own, without waiting for orders
senses.definitionCN: 不等指令便自行判断和行动的能力
senses.example: Solving the customer complaint showed real initiative.
senses.exampleCN: 主动解决顾客投诉体现了真正的主动性。
senses.why: From the root meaning beginning, initiative is the power to begin things yourself.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是「开始」，主动性正是自己发起事情的能力。

senses.title: The leading position in an activity
senses.definition: the advantage or control that comes from being the one who acts first
senses.definitionCN: 因率先行动而占据的优势或掌控地位
senses.example: The visiting team seized the initiative early in the match.
senses.exampleCN: 客队早早抢占了比赛的主动权。
senses.why: Whoever begins first steers the flow, so beginning becomes holding the lead.
senses.whyCN: 谁先开始谁就引导节奏，「开始」便转化为「掌控」。

senses.title: A new plan or proposal
senses.definition: an important new plan intended to solve a problem or achieve a goal
senses.definitionCN: 为解决问题或达成目标而提出的重要新计划
senses.example: The city launched a recycling initiative last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市去年春天发起了一项回收计划。
senses.why: A plan is a proposed beginning, so the beginning-word names the plan itself.
senses.whyCN: 计划就是一种提议的「开端」，于是「开端」一词转指计划本身。

senses.title: The power or right to propose new law
senses.definition: in politics, the right of citizens to propose a law directly
senses.definitionCN: 政治上公民直接提出法案的权利
senses.example: Voters used their initiative power to put the measure on the ballot.
senses.exampleCN: 选民动用立法倡议权把这项措施推上选票。
senses.why: Lawmaking from below is the citizenry acting as the first mover.
senses.whyCN: 自下而上立法，正是公民扮演「第一推动者」。

intro.en: Initiative traces straight back to Latin words about entering and beginning.
intro.cn: initiative 直接溯源于拉丁语中关于「进入、开始」的词。

items.en: From Latin initiare (to begin), built on initium (a beginning, an entrance), literally a going-in.
items.cn: 源自拉丁语 initiare（开始），建立在 initium（开端、入口）之上，字面为「走进去」。

items.en: Initium joined inire (to go in) with the prefix in-, so beginning was pictured as stepping in.
items.cn: initium 由前缀 in- 加 inire（走入）构成，「开始」被想象为「迈入」。

items.en: French coined initiative in the eighteenth century for the first move in a process or dispute.
items.cn: 法语于十八世纪造出 initiative，指进程或争端中的先手动作。

items.en: English borrowed it in the late eighteenth century, quickly adding the political-plan senses.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪末借入，很快衍生出政治与计划层面的义项。

items.en: Business and government usage fixed the two modern cores: personal drive and official program.
items.cn: 商务与政务用法固定了现代两大核心：个人主动性与官方计划。

note.en: All the look-alikes share the begin-root; the near-meaning words describe acting first.
note.cn: 形近词共享「开始」词根；近义词描述率先行动。

entries.definition: happening at the beginning
entries.definitionCN: 最初的；同根词

entries.definition: to begin or start something
entries.definitionCN: 开始；发起

entries.definition: the act of starting something or admitting someone
entries.definitionCN: 开始；入会仪式

entries.definition: energy and determination to act
entries.definitionCN: 干劲；进取心

entries.definition: willingness to attempt new things
entries.definitionCN: 进取精神；事业心

entries.definition: a plan put forward for consideration
entries.definitionCN: 提案；倡议方案

normalIntro.en: Five links built from the real root and word family.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词根与词族的联想。

normal.en: init- root means beginning; -ative turns it into a quality of tending to begin.
normal.cn: 词根 init- 表示开始；后缀 -ative 使之成为「倾向于开始」的品质。

normal.en: Same root: initial, initiate, initiation.
normal.cn: 同根词：initial、initiate、initiation。

normal.en: Take the initiative: be the one who begins.
normal.cn: take the initiative：做那个先开始的人。

normal.en: Government initiatives are plans that begin new programs.
normal.cn: 政府 initiative 是开启新项目的计划。

normal.en: Latin picture: initium, a stepping-in, like a foot through a doorway.
normal.cn: 拉丁画面：initium，迈入门槛，像一脚跨进门。

abstract.en: A chess player moving a pawn before the opponent has sat down.
abstract.cn: 对手尚未落座，棋手已推起了兵。

abstract.en: A raised hand in a quiet meeting room.

intro.en: Injure comes from a Latin word meaning to act unjustly toward someone.
intro.cn: injure 源自拉丁语，本义是「对某人行不义之事」。

items.en: Latin injurare meant to do wrong to, formed from in- (not) plus jurare (to swear, take an oath).
items.cn: 拉丁语 injurare 意为「亏待、加害」，由 in-（不）加 jurare（起誓）构成。

items.en: The oath root goes back to ius (law, right), so injustice was swearing against the right.
items.cn: 起誓词根回溯到 ius（法律、正当），不义即违背正当而起誓。

items.en: Old French carried the word as injurier, still with legal and wrongful overtones.
items.cn: 古法语传为 injurier，仍带法律与不义的色彩。

items.en: English adopted it in the fifteenth century, first about doing wrong to a person or their rights.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪引入，最初指亏待人或其权利。

items.en: The physical-wound sense became dominant in later centuries, especially in accidents and sport.
items.cn: 后世身体受伤义成为主导，常见于事故与体育语境。

note.en: Look-alikes keep the Latin law-root; near-meaning verbs differ in degree and object.

intro.en: Innocent says it in Latin: not-harming.
intro.cn: innocent 用拉丁语道明本义：不加害。

items.en: Latin innocens meant not injuring, from in- (not) plus nocere (to harm).
items.cn: 拉丁语 innocens 意为「不加害」，由 in-（不）加 nocere（伤害）构成。

items.en: Church writers used the word for moral purity and sinlessness.
items.cn: 教会作家用该词指道德纯洁、无罪污。

items.en: Old French borrowed it as innocent with both legal and moral shades.
items.cn: 古法语借入 innocent，兼具法律与道德两重色彩。

items.en: English took the word in the thirteenth century, early on often about simple folk.
items.cn: 英语十三世纪引入，早期多形容质朴之人。

items.en: Law fixed the not-guilty sense; everyday speech favors the naive and harmless senses.
items.cn: 法律固定了「无罪」义；日常口语偏爱「天真」与「无害」义。

note.en: The nocere root family warns of harm; near-words share purity or guiltlessness.
note.cn: nocere 词根家族皆与「害」有关；近义词共享纯真或无咎之意。
